#1981. Wolverhampton Wanderers vs Charlton Athletic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 19 Nov 2026 12:07

Wolverhampton Wanderers play host to Charlton Athletic on Saturday afternoon looking for the win that would keep the club in contention for top spot in the Championship table.

At a time when the West Midlands outfit sit in fourth place, Charlton's much-needed victory before the international break has moved them into 17th position.

Although some Wolves fans were disappointed with a 1-1 draw at Wrexham before the two-week break, Cesar Peixoto is currently doing an excellent job at Molineux.

Fourteen points have been collected from Wolves' last six matches to keep them one point adrift of leaders Birmingham City.

Furthermore, Wolves have not conceded more than one goal in any of those fixtures, while four points were accumulated from away contests at Bristol City and Wrexham before the international break.

Wolves now have 14 points from eight away games, the second-best record in the division, but they have only scored one goal in four of their most recent five matches at Molineux.

That will be a cause for concern for Peixoto, whose could still potentially move into first place this weekend if results go their way.

Meanwhile, Nathan Jones effectively kept himself in a job at Charlton with victory in their most recent fixture.

The 2-1 win at home to Sheffield United ended a run of 11 matches without success in the Championship, a run stretching back to August 29.

Charlton sit seven points adrift of the playoffs and seven points above the relegation zone courtesy of their win over the Blades.

Despite the London side registering just one away success in seven such fixtures this campaign, that solitary triumph came at relegated Premier League team West Ham United.

Wolverhampton Wanderers Championship form:

Kieran Trippier, Yerson Mosquera and Hugo Bueno could all be recalled to the Wolves defence.

With Fer Lopez and Jean-Ricner Bellegarde both missing international duty due to minor injuries, they are doubts for this fixture.

As Jordan James remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, Tommy Doyle is an option in central midfield, with Marshall Munetsi potentially being used further forward.

Matty Godden is expected to replace Charlie Kelman in the Charlton attack, reward for his decisive goal as a substitute versus Sheffield United.

Oliver Skipp and Harvey Knibbs will also come into contention for recalls, but the remainder of the starting XI could stay the same.

Wolverhampton Wanderers possible starting lineup:

Sa; Trippier, Mosquera, Krejci, Bueno; Andre, Doyle; R Gomes Munetsi, Mane; Armstrong

Charlton Athletic possible starting lineup:

Mannion; McNamara, Bindon, Koumetio, Bell; Coventry; Alli, Rankin-Costello, Knibbs, Campbell; Godden

With Charlton on a high after their win before the international break, they will back themselves to push Wolves, who have not always been convincing at Molineux. However, we can only predict a home win, albeit one by a narrower margin than many people will be anticipating.

At Manchester Magistrates’ Court, the 30-year-old pleaded not guilty to using threatening, abusive or insulting behaviour with intent to cause fear of, or provoke, unlawful violence.

He is alleged to have punched a Rochdale fan during a pitch invasion that took place when the two sides met in the National League on April 25.

York have offered their support to Boateng, who has been training ahead of Walsall’s visit tomorrow (November 21).

#1978. Barnsley FC 1 Sheffield Wednesday 2: Headstart costs Reds against clinical Owls

On a night dedicated to Weston Park's cancer work, the Reds extended that charity to their defending, and within 15 minutes, Wednesday already looked uncatchable.

Vimal Yoganathan's sixth goal in eight games ensured a proper South Yorkshire derby broke out, but the Reds are getting rather too good at nearly or semi-performances for their own comfort down in the League One relegation zone.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

After Yoganathan's strike, the home side showed the fight they should be a given in games against the near-neighbours, but it was already too late.

For the visitors, it was a character test passed in front of 5,700 invigilators in the away end, Jamal Lowe scoring from their only two shots on target on a night that felt like a big step forward for their new manager, Dave Challinor.

"Three points away ole, ole," sang the packed away end and more pertinently, "Wednesday are back."

Funny how one week can totally change the mood of a football club.

The Reds actually started the better, but they are getting good at looking good in ineffectual parts of the field, and awful at the business ends.

Their fans had been in mutinous mood before the game, hundreds gathering outside the ground before kick-off to protest about the way things are being run, but there was no such defiance when they needed it early on.

Lowe – playing more of an orthodox winger role with the balance of Wednesday's unchanged side titled more towards a back four than a three than it had been the previous week – was ruthless in exploiting it.

When Barry Bannan lofted a free-kick to the back post in the ninth minute, Liam Cooper was in far too much space there. The defender headed the ball across goal, and Lowe pounced for the Owls' third set-piece goal in a week.

Five minutes later, two passes took the visitors from the halfway line to a second goal.

Callum Slattery's pass to Bannan was almost cut out but when he found Lowe, but Jubril Okedina stood off, almost daring the forward to score, so he did.

Barnsley's early work lacked that conviction.

Reyes Cleary's second-minute snapshot lacked the power to beat Joe Lumley, and Ryan Brownlie's also allowed the goalkeeper to save. Makenzie Kirk miskicked a shot when Cleary picked him out, and when Patrick Kelly ran onto a knockdown by the centre-forward, his shot lacked power.

Cleary put a shot well wide and Luca Connell hammered one into Billy Mitchell.

Ziyad Larkeche controlled a fairly routine Cieran Slicker pass over the touchline.

But a side with seven starters under the age of 23 plugged away and got back into it courtesy of one of their young leaders.

Like Okedina, Yan Valery stood off Cleary and when the winger delivered a low cross, Yoganathan arrived onto it like a centre-forward to pull a goal back.

With both sides attacking their own noisy ends, it made for an entertaining second half.

Like Barnsley at the start of the first half, Wednesday pushed the harder, without making it count.

Bannan had a shot blocked and when Slicker came out of his goal to stop former Red Davis Keillor-Dunn finishing a Bannan pass, Lowe lifted his shot onto the roof of the net.

At the other end, Barnsley centre-back Sam Gale forced his way to the byline, but his cross cleared those in the area. Larkeche put an acrobatic effort wide.

It was Wednesday who were throwing on the substitutes - a sign of their deeper resources, but also off their keenness to finally add to Lowe's second shot on target, 14 minutes in.

Despite one of those substitutes, Harry Gray, accelerating past Gale for a chance Slattery had blocked, it never came, but it did not need to because hard as Barnsley pushed – throwing centre-back Connor O'Riordan on as a late emergency striker and sending Slicker up for a stoppage-time corner – they could not find the next goal either.

Luca Connell came the closest, his free-kick tipped over in the 93rd minute.

His team are just not good enough to gift promotion wannabes like Wednesday a two-goal headstart and get away with it. Only just, you might say, but game after game that is enough.

Barnsley: Slicker; Okedina (Reid 86), Gale, Kay, Larkeche; Connell, Kelly (Johnson 86); Brownlie (O'Riordan 90), Yoganathan (Noslin 81), Cleary; Kirk (Toure 81).

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Valery, Bernard (Santos 86), Cooper, Swinkels (Palmer 70); Heskey, Mitchell (Barry 70), Slattery, Bannan (Gray 78), J Lowe (Liongola 70); Keillor-Dunn.

#1977. Motherwell vs Rangers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 12:39, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 12:46

Returning to Scottish Premiership action for the first time in two weeks, Motherwell welcome an in-form Rangers side to Fir Park on Saturday afternoon.

The Well head into the fixture following a 1-1 draw away to Dundee United, while the Gers extended their unbeaten run in all competitions to 12 matches with a 2-0 victory over St Mirren, leaving them four points behind league leaders Celtic with a game in hand.

After an impressive fourth-placed finish in the Scottish Premiership last season under Jens Berthel Askou, Motherwell secured European football and earned widespread praise for their attacking style of play.

However, Askou left Fir Park over the summer to take charge of Toulouse, with the North Lanarkshire club appointing Swedish coach Alfred Johansson as his replacement, although he has so far struggled to build on the progress made during the 2025-26 campaign.

After 13 Scottish Premiership matches, the Well sit ninth in the table with three wins, four draws and six defeats, having conceded 21 goals, with only three sides shipping more, while just three teams have scored fewer than their 14.

Despite their worrying start to the new season, Motherwell entered the final international break of the year on the back of a three-match unbeaten run, with draws against St Johnstone and Dundee United either side of a narrow 1-0 victory over St Mirren on Halloween.

While that positive end to October and start to November has offered some encouragement to Johansson's side, they will know they must pick up where they left off before the two-week break to create more breathing room above the bottom two and close the gap on the teams higher up the table.

As for Rangers, they appear to have put their difficult start under Derek McInnes behind them, with the Gers heading into the busy festive period in a strong position to challenge for silverware and close in on rivals Celtic in the Premiership title race.

McInnes's side entered the break with a 2-0 away victory over St Mirren, courtesy of goals either side of half-time from Ryan Naderi and Dan Neil, extending their unbeaten run to 12 matches and marking their first defeat-free spell since August, which has also included two victories over their bitter Glasgow rivals.

This impressive turnaround has followed an early European exit and a difficult start to their domestic campaign under the former Hearts boss, but Rangers are now showing significant signs of improvement compared to recent seasons.

At this stage last year, the Gers were fourth in the table and had recently replaced Russell Martin with Danny Rohl, following another difficult managerial spell, while they had also been sitting third 12 months earlier, highlighting the progress McInnes has made since taking charge.

Despite their recent resurgence, Rangers remain four points behind Celtic, although a victory on Saturday would cut that gap to a single point, with a game in hand on the league leaders still to come.

The sides meet for the second time this season following Rangers' narrow 1-0 victory at Ibrox in early September, with the Gers having since turned their home ground into something of a fortress, as no side has taken a point off them there since their defeat on matchweek two.

Motherwell could name the same starting XI that drew 1-1 with Dundee United, although they remain without several first-team players through injury.

Alex Lowry, Johnny Koutroumbis and Dylan Williams are all expected to miss out due to knee, muscle and hamstring problems respectively, although the trio could return by the start of December.

Lukas Fadinger has scored twice in his last two appearances, albeit both goals coming from the penalty spot, and is expected to anchor the midfield while wearing the captain's armband once again.

Meanwhile, the visitors make the short journey south with a longer list of injury concerns, although they at least avoided any fresh setbacks during their victory over St Mirren.

McInnes will remain without Ross McCrorie, Cameron Devlin, Daisuke Yokota, Lawrence Shankland, Youssef Chermiti and Jose Cifuentes, although Chermiti is the only one of the injured players expected to remain sidelined into 2027.

Paulsen; Sparrow, Girdwood-Reich, Moormann, Longelo; Hodge, Fadinger; Maswanhise, Said, Kanga; Palmer-Houlden

Pandur; Sterling, Makhanya, Fernandez, Penrice; Bouanni, Neil, Raskin, Kim Min-Su; Naderi, Kelsy

Motherwell head into the fixture with some encouraging momentum after going three matches unbeaten, but we expect their progress to be halted by an in-form Rangers side, who should secure their ninth league victory of the season and further close the gap on Celtic.

#1976. £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Some surprised faces then when Moyes said later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”

The game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes said that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”

In the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

De Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender said: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and showed that mentality again in the second half.

“We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l

"Six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a DISGRACE" 😬Ashley Young says that the Spurs players will need to have conversations about their lack of threat going forward ❌ pic.twitter.com/0KNomGEavx

"Absolutely diabolical" 😬Jamie Redknapp on Spurs not scoring in their first four Premier League games 😳 pic.twitter.com/48Nbxymlev

Tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

Boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh

Dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

There will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

Jordan Pickford gets down well to deny Lucas Bergvall! 🧤 pic.twitter.com/59uoHTqto6

Tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

Garner is booked after he clatters into Savio. Everton have produced a tough and disciplined defensive perfomance so far.

Spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a big chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

De Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

Johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

That opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

That was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

"What a chance this was!"Brennan Johnson had the chance to put Everton in front against his former club 😯 pic.twitter.com/fUi7t6hX7t

Everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts quickly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

What is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

Antonín Kinský redeems himself after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall fails to take advantage! 😮 pic.twitter.com/nuKZju90Wz

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

Enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

The start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors currently have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

George does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

Spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

Ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

We are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

An uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

There will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

There has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

That is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

Tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

Gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

Spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Big question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

Tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

Spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

As expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

Greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

"Solanke is a crucial player"Roberto De Zerbi on the importance of Dominic Solanke being fit for Spurs 💪 pic.twitter.com/FNWNsTWdt8

Coventry City vs Brighton & Hove Albion (14:00)

Manchester United vs Manchester City (16:30)

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

The Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” says Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

🎧🫡 Thierno Barry ahead of today's clash in North London. pic.twitter.com/mwlsKH8Pid

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van de Ven, Van Hecke, Robertson; Tonali, Bentancur, Fernandes; Savio, Solankem, Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Tel, Bergvall, Kudus, Davies.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

After scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @SpursOfficial. COYB! ✊#TOTEVE pic.twitter.com/mOcCayRUfm

Roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1975. Andriy Shevchenko demands apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk over ‘baseless’ failed drugs test claims

Andriy Shevchenko has demanded an apology from Chelsea winger Mykhailo Mudryk after he blamed Ukraine’s national team for his failed drugs test.

Mudryk, who is on loan at Tottenham Hotspur from Chelsea, was suspended from November 2024 to July 2026 after he tested positive for the banned substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old initially faced a four-year ban but returned to football this summer after he accepted that he had breached anti-doping rules and agreed to a suspension equal to the time he had already served.

Speaking to YouTube channel Guest of Gordon this week, Mudryk was asked who he felt was to blame for the adverse finding.

‘The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team,’ Mudryk said.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘It should never have existed. I probably haven’t said it publicly yet but I’m saying it now.

‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.’

Asked how meldonium got into his system, Mudryuk said: ‘The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system. At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team.

‘There are people who keep an eye on it. In the Ukrainian national team we have a nutritionist who hands us pills every couple of days before games. He brings us a little cup. Everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Former Chelsea striker Shevchenko, who is now the president of the Ukrainian Association of Football, has hit back at Mudryk’s claims and has described the winger’s version of events as ‘baseless slander’.

‘I want to express my position on the accusations of Mykhailo Mudryk. Loud statements were made about the UAF, the Ukrainian national team. This is a baseless slander against our people, who do their job honestly and professionally,’ Shevchenko said in a statement to Tribuna Ukraine.

‘Instead, after the suspension of Mykhailo Mudryk, his representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to artificially find an employee who would take responsibility for the appearance of meldonium in his doping sample.

‘The UAF refused – such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work. The accusations from Mykhailo’s representatives were not confirmed or proven after many studies and inspections. The investigation and the final settlement agreement with WADA and the English association confirm this.

‘After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during the national team training camp. The team staff complied with this request.

‘Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also agreed for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him during the training camp. These people monitored his regimen and recovery and helped him with his daily life.

‘The UAF has completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk’s representatives with the information they requested and have been in contact with those who worked on the case.

‘I know people who have been working in the national team for many years. I trust them, because during all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make one doubt their professionalism

‘If Mykhailo has evidence to support his words, let him provide it. If there is no such evidence, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he questioned.’

#1974. Dave Challinor on why he thought Sheffield Wednesday's early lead backfired against Barnsley FC

Two goals inside the opening quarter of an hour from Jamal Lowe ought to have seen the Owls to a comfortable victory over opponents who have now not won in ten League One games.

But they did not have another shot on target all night, and were made to sweat it out on a freezing cold night to claim a 2-1 victory.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"You've always got to work hard," said Challinor, who was taking charge of his first League One away game as Owls manager.

"The players probably felt we didn't work hard enough in the first half. After going after going in front, sometimes it's the worst thing can happen because players think the game's done and we can now sit back and not have to have to defend with the personnel we've got on the pitch.

"Us defending in a block with looking to break with Slatts (Callum Slattery) and Davis (Keillor-Dunn) and Barry Bannan doesn't really work for us, so we need to be more aggressive, high up the pitch, and expose ourselves. We didn't do that, it'll take time.

"I'll own that in terms of what it looks like but that's where we need to get to.

"We've got to at that point really be on the neck of people and go and get the third goal, not be comfortable thinking two is an easy night for us because you allow a young team to get some momentum and come back into the game."

But as critical as he was of areas of the first-half performance, Challinor was delighted with the spirt he saw in his new players in the second half.

"We've got we've got a group that want to defend right across the board," he said. "We've done some work this week around emergency defending.

"You're not going to get much better than Coops (Liam Cooper), Sil (Swinkels), Dish (Di'Shon Bernard), Yan (Valery) and Rico (Ricardo Santos).

"They want to block, they want to get themselves in the way.

"We were a little bit better second half.

"We had a really good chat at half time. I told them what I felt, we'd just got to make better decisions.

"We've got we've got an experienced group, but some of our decision-making in that last half an hour caused us more problems than it should have.

"If it's a derby, you need to be able to be 100 per cent because Barnsley, at that point, are going for it, are open, and two or three passes, we could have we could have been in a lot more often, and we made the wrong decision at the wrong time.

"Winning's a brilliant habit, but I'm very realistic about the work that needs to be done.

"I never have been a great winner, as daft as that sounds. My job's to be analytical and understand where we get better.

"I want them to enjoy winning. I've said that to them. I want it to be absolutely bouncing because winning's a brilliant feeling and a brilliant habit to get into.

"They found a way when maybe not performed the best. There's loads more to come from this group. My job is to make sure that happens.

"You're always going to be try and be a perfectionist as a football coach. You'll never get to that but that doesn't mean you stop trying."

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It left coach Stendel downbeat when he addressed the media after the game.

When asked if he thought the first 15 minutes had decided the game, Stendel replied: "I would wouldn't say the first 15 minutes was two situations, and I know you would think, 'What you do in training?' but we talked exactly that about this, especially the second goal after last week.

"We prepared the team especially for a situation like this yesterday (Thursday). We do it in training.

"But yeah, when you do not defend the ball with the last desire, then you concede a goal like this, and this was hard.

"The support was really good but 2-0 down after 15 minutes in a game like this is hard against a team with so much quality.

"After the second goal, we have the feeling only we played in the game but we only scored one goal, and we talk again about the defeat in the game that we don't have to lose."

Both Jamal Lowe's goals were very preventable from Barnsley perspective.

"It's not the quality from Sheffield, our defending in two situations decided the game," lamented Stendel.

"We all said we played a good game but we have to do it better.

"We talk a lot in the season about situations like that.

"Everybody can see that the players never give up, we really have a good character in the squad, a lot of power, and we can play at 2-0 down against one from the top teams in the league.

"We lose by only on one goal a lot of times.

"It showed we have a good mentality in the group, but everybody - not only the players, not only supporters, everybody needs a positive result in the league."

#1972. Liverpool: Why Brajan Gruda would be perfect Mo Salah successor

By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 12:41

Brajan Gruda has been one of the revelations of the start of the season with Leipzig and Germany. His profile appears ideal to strengthen Liverpool’s attack.

An attacking midfielder by training, Brajan Gruda is shining at the start of the season as a right winger. After a disappointing spell at Brighton, the 22-year-old German bounced back last winter at RB Leipzig. He has been loaned this season by the English club to the German side. Leipzig will sign him permanently in 2027 for £25.5m (€30m). Gruda will then receive a contract until June 2031.

That transfer does not mean he will stay long at Leipzig, however. According to Sky Sport Germany, Bayern Munich have the Germany international on their shortlist. The Bavarian club have not planned any move in this case, unless Michael Olise were to leave. It must be said that, all things considered, the profiles of the two players are quite similar.

Beyond the fact that they are left-footed number 10s shining on the right side of the attack, they are technical players who are rather fond of assists. Brajan Gruda is the fourth player in Europe’s top five leagues with the most successful dribbles at the start of this season, with 36.

He is very efficient in this area, succeeding with 70.6% of his dribbles, a better ratio than Lamine Yamal (58.3%) or Kylian Mbappe (59.7%), who nevertheless attempt more. Beyond dribbles, the 22-year-old is also decisive, with two goals scored and five assists delivered in 13 games for Leipzig.

Those performances opened the doors of the Germany national team. Jurgen Klopp did not hesitate to give him his first two caps, starting him against Serbia (3-1 win) and the Netherlands (5-0) during this November international break. Gruda shone with a solo goal against the Serbs, as well as another goal and two assists against the Dutch.

His feat against Serbia impressed his manager. ‘It’s completely crazy. The defender in front of him? Poor guy!’ - the German manager exclaimed.

On the pitch, in those two games, his understanding with Florian Wirtz, playing as number 10, was also highlighted. Could the two men therefore be reunited at Liverpool?

Liverpool did not sign a genuine right winger this summer, after the departure of Mohamed Salah. Left-footed, technical and provocative, Brajan Gruda has an interesting profile to replace the Egyptian star. He is capable of long solo runs and of shining in tight spaces, relying on his silky left foot. He is a player who has emerged in recent months.

Liverpool therefore seem to have every interest in quickly getting their hands on the Leipzig player. Indeed, if he continues to perform at this level, his market value, which stands at £23.8m (€28m), should rise considerably, while new European heavyweights, in addition to Bayern Munich, will take an interest in his profile.

In this case, Liverpool have two allies who could push Brajan Gruda to join the English giants: Florian Wirtz and Jurgen Klopp.

#1970. Swansea City vs West Bromwich Albion - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:37

Life without Vitor Matos begins for Swansea City on Saturday afternoon, when fellow promotion hopefuls West Bromwich Albion visit Swansea.com Stadium for a Championship battle.

The Swans have lost their Portuguese mastermind to Ligue 1 following a poor run of form prior to the international break, whereas the Baggies come into this South Wales clash full of confidence.

After being linked to vacant roles at Crystal Palace and Sporting Lisbon over the past month, Swansea head coach Matos has been poached by Ligue 1 outfit Strasbourg, leaving the Welsh side without a permanent manager this weekend.

The 38-year-old's departure comes after an overall impressive start to the season for the Swans, however, they have lost four of their past five second-tier matches, falling to defeat by Birmingham City on November 7.

Collecting just three points from Matos's final five games at the helm, Swansea have slid down to sixth place in the Championship standings after 15 matches, still just three points behind the league leaders.

Alarmingly, a once-watertight defence has conceded 11 goals across its last five contests in the second tier, although the Swans were excellent in their most recent home match, smashing Blackburn Rovers by a 4-0 scoreline.

Former Swansea defender Ashley Williams is expected to join Leon Britton and Kris O'Leary in an interim coaching group on Saturday afternoon, when the hosts will look to extend their unbeaten home run against West Brom to eight matches.

Concerns regarding a potential relegation to League One in the spring feel a million miles away from The Hawthorns right now, with West Brom targeting an unlikely promotion push at the top of the Championship.

Since losing to pacesetters Birmingham on October 10, the Baggies have strung together an impressive six-match unbeaten run (W4 D2) in the second tier, enjoying a standout home success last time out.

James Morrison's troops took full advantage of a wounded Lions pack in the Black Country on November 7, when Isaac Price, Jayson Molumby and Norway international Felix Horn Myhre all netted in the demolition of Millwall.

Yet to be defeated by a club below them in the league standings so far this season, West Brom are currently occupying fifth position, just a single point behind Blues, Middlesbrough and Stoke City at the summit of the division.

The Albion were simply awful on the road during the opening months of 2026 but have improved massively under the stewardship of Morrison, who has masterminded wins at Wrexham (2-1) and West Ham United (3-1) over the past few weeks.

Swansea were unsuccessful in their appeal of Marko Stamenic's red card at Birmingham prior to the international pause.

As a result, the New Zealander is sidelined for the next three matches, including the South Wales derby against Cardiff City on November 29.

Goncalo Franco and Stephen Welsh are both doubts for this weekend's game due to muscular problems.

West Brom suffered a major fitness blow during the two-week break, with influential midfielder Ousmane Diakite picking up a calf injury whilst on duty for Mali.

The much-improved 26-year-old faces at least eight weeks on the sidelines, joining fellow midfielder Toby Collyer in the medical room.

The Baggies are also short on options in defence, with Noah Galves (knee) out of action, but captain George Campbell is available for selection.

Vigouroux; Lissah, Cabango, Seelt, Tymon; Widell, Fulton, Iorpenda; Yeo, Eom, Idah

West Bromwich Albion possible starting lineup:

O'Leary; Pereira, Mepham, Phillips, Styles; Whitwell, Molumby, Nzingoula, Price; Heggebo, Morgan

Rocked by the sudden departure of Matos, Swansea will be chasing home comforts in South Wales this weekend.

Even without Diakite, West Brom should be good enough for a share of the spoils with the managerless Swans.

#1969. GdS: 3-4-2-1 or 3-4-1-2 – how Amorim’s formation could change with January addition

AC Milan are tempted by the idea of signing Endrick and Nicolo Tresoldi, but how would Ruben Amorim’s system change?

There has been plenty of talk about January signings, but as much as they would be good to bring, they have to be the right fit. After all, signing a name without thinking ahead will only be problematic. So, the right calculations must be made by Amorim and the recruitment team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This morning, Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) looked at how Amorim’s system could change with the arrival of Endrick or Tresoldi and it’s a pretty simple idea.

With Endrick, there would be ‘fewer adjustments’ thanks to his versatility and also his ability to play in the formation already. So, it would see him playing behind the striker alongside Christian Pulisic or Alphadjo Cisse.

For Tresoldi’s arrival, things would have to change. He’s played most of his career as a lone striker, but that would probably change. Instead, he’d probably make up a two-man strike force, alongside Ramos, and then Christian Pulisic or Alphadjo Cisse would play behind him.

It’s a logical choice, but it would mean Amorim would have to change his ideas mid-season. Ultimately, the mercato will choose the route of the Portuguese’s team.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

For either of those two formations to work, we first need proper wingbacks. And define the midfield. Because here’s the catch, I don’t really get – does he want to play wingbacks or inverted wingbacks on the flanks?

Because that too defines the midfield. Playing with regular wingbacks doesn’t require so much defensive cover in the middle as the wingbacks add to the density there. Final third is reserved for inverted playmakers and a striker. Playing inverted wingbacks, that’s a different story. Inverted wingbacks are usually more attacking oriented and as such like to push higher up and get involved in the last third. That exposes the midfield. And this is the version Amorim plays as his strategy is to overload opponents half and penalty area from the flanks inside.

So in any case we’re potentially short on either the flanks or in midfield. And here I don’t see Athekane taking the LWB spot as an inverted wingback like suggested in some reports. He’s not an inverted wingback and will just be wasted.

Amorim’s wingbacks aren’t inverted though… that’s why he doesn’t use Alexis as LWB

Amorim wants his wingbacks to be good in 1v1 and be able to beat the defender. He doesn’t use Alexis as a LWB because Alexis isn’t good in 1v1.

For years having no clear identity and building squads to match no system have caused a mess.

#1968. Manchester United shortlist £26m Spurs target to solve Mauricio Pochettino issue

Manchester United are considering a move for Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic in the January transfer window, according to reports.

Mauricio Pochettino arrived at United this week having replaced Michael Carrick, who was sacked during the international break.

But the Argentine begins his tenure at Old Trafford without a recognised striker as Benjamin Sesko is sidelined until next year due to a shin injury.

United have made funds available to strengthen Pochettino’s squad in January and the club are targeting a new striker.

According to The i Paper, Matanovic is on United’s striker shortlist alongside Folarin Balogun, who Monaco are open to selling in the January transfer window.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The report adds that United are also looking to bolster Pochettino’s defence with Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey and left-back Antonee Robinson under consideration.

Matanovic, meanwhile, was signed by Freiburg in an €8 million (£6.8m) deal from Eintracht Frankfurt last year.

The Croatia international, who offers a physical presence in attack at 6ft 5in, has scored 23 goals in 64 games for Freiburg so far.

At international level, Matanovic has scored two goals in 17 appearances for Croatia and came off the bench in three games at the World Cup in the summer.

Matanovic, who is now valued at around €30m (£26m), has also been linked with a move to Tottenham.

When asked about his future in September, Matanovic insisted he had not received an approach to leave Freiburg.

‘As for me, I’m currently in Freiburg. There has been absolutely no contact with anyone from my side,’ the striker said.

#1967. Sevilla vs Real Betis - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 13:21

The latest instalment of the Seville derby will take place at Estadio Ramon on Saturday evening, as Sevilla and Real Betis lock horns in La Liga.

Sevilla have historically dominated this fixture, but Real Betis have had the better of the recent meetings between the two, losing just one of their last eight contests with the White and Reds.

Sevilla have a record of five wins, three draws and four defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 18 points leaving them in sixth position in the La Liga table.

Luis Garcia Plaza's side have only picked up one point from their last two league games, though, losing at Getafe at the start of November before drawing 0-0 with Alaves in their last fixture in front of their own fans before the international break.

Los Nervionenses have not managed to finish fourth in Spain's top flight since 2021-22, and there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a difficult few seasons for the club, finishing 12th, 14th, 17th and 13th in their last four campaigns.

However, Sevilla are currently showing form that could see them claim a European finish, which would be a major step forward given their recent troubles.

The White and Reds have won 61, lost 39 and drawn 35 of their previous 135 matches against Real Betis in all competitions, with their last success over their Seville rivals coming at home in October 2024.

Real Betis have claimed seven points from the last three league matches against Sevilla, including a 2-0 victory at Estadio Ramon last season, while they have lost just once to their rivals since February 2022.

Manuel Pellegrini's side recorded a 2-0 win over Elche in their last league match on November 8, before beating Navalcarnero 3-2 in the Copa del Rey four days later.

El Glorioso have won eight, drawn two and lost two of their 12 league matches this season to collect 26 points, which has left them in fourth spot in the division, eight points ahead of Sevilla leading into this weekend's Seville derby.

It has been a busy opening few months of the season for Real Betis given that Pellegrini's team are also playing in the Champions League; a strong start to their league stage has left them 11th in the table, claiming nine points from four matches.

The Seville team finished fifth in Spain's top flight last season and will again be expecting to challenge for a spot high up the division this term.

Sevilla will welcome Manu Bueno back into their squad on Saturday following a suspension, but Marcao, Peque and Miguel Sierra are again likely to miss out through injury.

Ruben Vargas is also a doubt due to the issue that forced him off against Alaves, which could mean that Chidera Ejuke is introduced into the starting side.

Robbie Ure is pushing to be introduced at centre-forward, but a tough start to his career with Sevilla has seen him manage just one goal in 12 league appearances.

Real Betis, meanwhile, remain without the services of Facundo Bernal through suspension.

Diego Llorente and Cucho Hernandez are also major doubts for the visitors on Saturday.

Troy Parrott is expected to continue through the middle for the away side, while Isco and Antony are also likely to retain their positions in the first XI.

Vlachodimos; Iglesias, Sangante, Salas, Suazo; Fofana, Agoume; Ejuke, Romero, Correia; Stassin

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, Garcia; Fornals, Roca; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Parrott

This is a tough match to call, especially off the back of an international break. Cases can be made for either side to win it, but we believe that a tight match will finish all square.

#1966. Thomas Tuchel's 'best night' as England manager: Three Lions boss hails heroes after Spain victory - but hits out at Elliot Anderson decision made by referee he previously labelled a 'one out of 10'

Published: 18:10 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 19:58 EST, 15 November 2026

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss

'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'

#1965. The Premier League’s newest managers have a lot to lose

Farewell then, Michael Carrick and Pierre Sage, who have gone off to the great big Premier League managerial scrapheap in the sky after an international break where only the identity of the next James Bond could rival speculation over Carrick’s eventual replacement in particular.

In Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank respectively, Manchester United and Crystal Palace have gone for a pair of managers whose reputations in English football could do with a good start this weekend to avoid the varying levels of doom that have surrounded Old Trafford and Selhurst Park from peaking again.

It’s a good thing, then, that despite their contrasting styles, both are known for putting emphasis on energy – not just in how their team plays on the pitch, but in how the culture around the club feels off it.

Pochettino has made headlines before for his love of lemons (they absorb negative energy, he’ll have you know) and his apparent sixth sense. In his 2017 book Brave New World, he wrote: ‘What most influences my decisions is my ability to see if the right energy is flowing.’

What kind of energy he felt flowing through director of football Jason Wilcox is anyone’s guess at this stage, but his emphasis on things like togetherness and the mindset of his players could finally be the key to starting to turn the Suez canal tanker that United have become, on the pitch at least.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

If Pochettino comes across as part high-level manager, part yoga teacher, then Frank has the air of an executive ready to rebuild the culture at an ailing business.

A year off from football was on the cards after he was sacked by Tottenham in February. The Dane turned down Palace during the summer in favour of World Cup punditry and attending the Tour de France, and didn’t sound completely convinced he’d made the right decision to cut that break short.

‘I was a little bit, “When do I want to go back in? Is it now?” Then this opportunity came up,’ he told PalaceTV this week. ‘I was thinking, this is probably too good to turn down. When I’m sitting here, walking around the training ground, it was just, “Okay, you’re back”, which scared me a little bit, but it’s good.’ Consider the troops rallied.

Questions surround the suitability of both appointments, as Pochettino’s biggest success at Spurs was built on the back of a young, mobile team with something to prove and Frank’s at Brentford came as part of a well-oiled machine. You’d be waiting a long time for anyone to describe United or Palace as either of those these days.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

There’s hope to be found too, for those willing to look for it. Frank did only really have half a bad season and the perceived wisdom is that his personality will suit a ‘smaller’ club – as long as he stays away from any Brighton-branded coffee cups – while of all the managers tasked with fixing United, Pochettino does have the air of a man who can become a messianic figure.

Managerial reputations can only survive a certain number of kicks before there’s no coming back and there may not be many chances left for either man at this level if things go pear-shaped.

However, with both teams playing pretty much every three days for the next month, there are plenty of opportunities for their new managers to shift the vibes back towards a positive setting.

And even if the wins don’t start flowing, transfer enthusiasts should have something to cling on to as Palace and United are reportedly ready to back their new men with some signings once the January window opens.

It’s nice to have something to look forward to after Christmas, at least.
