#1860. Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

This particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

So to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

“I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a big career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

As impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”

Allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has said supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca said.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

With the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:

Erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

Great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Big cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

What a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:

And without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

Samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

He has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

Samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic shows some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

Spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a new five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

Speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

Keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

His older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Joao Pedro is still not fit to face Leeds United this weekend, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has revealed.

The Blues have been unable to call on the striker since his shock omission from their starting lineup for last month’s 2-0 home defeat to Tottenham.

The Brazilian had picked up a thigh injury in training and has not represented the west Londoners since.

During that time, Chelsea’s form has dipped as a result and they have lost to both Spurs and Sunderland in the Premier League as well as being eliminated from the Carabao Cup by Liverpool on penalties.

Joao Pedro also sat out of Brazil duty during the international break.

Chelsea’s plan had always been to wait until the return of club football following the international window and then reassess the 25-year-old’s situation.

On Friday afternoon, Alonso provided a fresh update on Joao Pedro’s recovery as he previewed his side’s home league fixture against Daniel Farke’s Leeds on Saturday.

“Not yet,” the Spaniard replied when asked about his No9.

“He’s not ready to train yet for the team. Not for Leeds no. We need to see day by day how he is feeling.”

Chelsea will also be without summer signing Maxence Lacroix, who picked up a hamstring injury in the loss at Anfield.

Standard Sport reported previously that the Blues fear he could be out until the turn of the year.

“He is not ready to play for tomorrow and is a similar situation to Joao,” Alonso said of the French international.

#1858. GdS: Worth the price tag – how Moreira became ‘untouchable’ for Milan and Belgium

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby shows, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

He set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Moreira is currently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

With four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

#1857. Roberto De Zerbi sends Mykhailo Mudryk clear message after Spurs star’s Arsenal transfer admission

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Roberto De Zerbi has said that Mykhailo Mudryk has his full confidence, but must work hard to change the trajectory of his loan spell at Tottenham after a difficult start to life in north London.

Mudryk joined Spurs on a season-long loan from Chelsea on the final day of the summer transfer window, with the club having a £75million option to buy the Ukrainian international at the end of the season.

Mudryk was suspended from competitive football from November 2024 until July 2026 after testing positive for the banned substance meldonium, but it had been hoped he could resurrect his career under De Zerbi.

The pair worked together during Mudryk’s formative years at Shakhtar Donetsk, with the 25-year-old calling De Zerbi his “football father”.

Mudryk, though, has not got going in a Spurs shirt after suffering an ankle ligament injury in training in September.

He had been targeting a return in Spurs’ next two games, but now appears to have suffered a setback after De Zerbi confirmed he would not be available against Ipswich this weekend.

“No, because the plan was to play Ipswich or Sunderland, or any way to be available,” De Zerbi stated when asked if he would be back to face Ipswich.

“He felt no pain, but not comfortable last week. And they take two weeks more, and step by step we’re going to see the situation.”

To make matters worse, Mudryk appeared on the Ukrainian podcast ‘Guest of Gordon’ this week and stated that before joining Chelsea in January 2023, he had wanted to join Spurs’ arch-rivals Arsenal before adding that he was using his loan at Spurs to build fitness ahead of a return to Chelsea next summer.

Asked about the comments, De Zerbi said he understood why Spurs fans would be frustrated and asked Mudryk to show his qualities on the pitch.

“Yes, I can understand the fans, but Mudryk is a good guy, he’s a good player,” De Zerbi continued.

“He suffered a lot for the situation in the last couple of years. He has just one thing to do, show on the pitch his qualities, show on the pitch that now he’s playing for Tottenham. Tottenham is a big club, like the other clubs, not less at all.”

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 18:59, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:20

Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu both trained with Manchester United on Thursday, with the Red Devils preparing for Sunday's Premier League clash against Liverpool.

Dorgu made his return from a muscular injury in Man United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa before the November international break.

However, the left-back did not feature for Denmark during the international period, having been deemed not ready by the national team's doctor.

“We have carried out a series of tests on Dorgu, and he has not performed well enough to be ready to play in the two matches," said Denmark team doctor Morten Boesen.

Naturally, there had been concern surrounding Dorgu and his involvement in the clash at Anfield this weekend.

However, Man United have confirmed that the defender featured in Thursday's training session, suggesting that he will be involved in Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the 20-time English champions.

Maguire was also involved, with the experienced centre-back seemingly recovering from the back injury that forced him off the field against Villa.

Lisandro Martinez will also be free to return to the squad, having served a suspension against Villa, but it appears unlikely that Luke Shaw will be involved.

Benjamin Sesko, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte are definitely out, while Marcus Rashford needs to be assessed due to a hip problem.

Pochettino will hold his pre-Liverpool press conference on Friday afternoon, where he will provide an update on the team's injury situation.

"I think it's an opportunity," Pochettino told MUTV in his first interview. "It's a privilege to be, you know, head coach of Manchester United and I think we cannot waste time.

"We need to be ready to compete [on] Sunday. Now it’s not time to think about rest, it’s not time to think about sleep. It’s about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield."

Man United have only won one of their 10 matches in England's top flight this term, and they currently sit down in 18th spot in the Premier League table.

#1855. Manchester United chief delivers surprise verdict on summer transfers amid relegation fears

Omar Berrada insists Manchester United’s squad has been made “fundamentally better” by its summer transfers, despite sitting in the relegation zone after ten matches.

The Red Devils have endured a historically poor start to the campaign, which earlier this month resulted in the sacking of head coach Michael Carrick.

The club’s transfer business in recent years has been heavily criticised, and another uninspiring summer has done little to cool fan frustrations. While glaring issues in defence and attack went unaddressed, United spent around £155m to add Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba to the midfield.

The quality and price of those transfers have both been questioned, particularly as none of the three has particularly impressed in the early days of this campaign, with United having won just one league outing by late November.

Club CEO Berrada, though, insists the squad is in a better place now than it was in May, saying inflated transfer fees made it difficult to navigate the summer transfer window.

Speaking in a rare interview with Sky Sports, he explained: "When we look at this summer, we went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play. It's probably been the summer or the transfer window where there's been the highest inflation in transfer fees.

"And we've said publicly and we've said consistently in the last few years that we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players for the right value at the right time in terms of what the squad needs.

"And when we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we're receiving a lot of criticism for it, but we're actually happy with the players that we bought.

"We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, and Karl Darlow - and let's not forget that we've also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona - these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.”

Come the end of last season, United’s back line appeared to be the area most in need of updating, with the current corps ageing and underperforming.

Berrada, though, felt the squad had sufficient numbers in defence already, which allowed him to focus on bolstering the midfield.

“There’s a lot of discussion about the back line,” he continued. “But we did come into it thinking: we have depth. We have nine players that can play in the back line, in the back four positions.

“So that's why we looked primarily at investing in the midfield. But we were always looking for opportunities. I think it's been widely reported that we were looking at potentially the left-back position as a reinforcement.

“So could we have signed an additional defender to strengthen the depth and the quality? Yes, but we have to find the right players and you have to find the right players at the right value.

“There's no point in us spending £40m, £50m for players that we're not convinced are going to add value to the team.

“So it's always about being disciplined and finding the right opportunities and getting the right players that are going to take us forward.”

Premier League football will soon resume after the international break, with Manchester City hoping to rectify their recent troubles against Fulham in Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

Since suffering their first loss of the Premier League season to Aston Villa, City have fallen to two further defeats at the hands of Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

With time to think over the international break, Enzo Maresca has decisions to make when it comes to his starting XI for the visit of Fulham to the Etihad this weekend.

#1853. How Vinicius Jr's lavish summer holiday has left him playing catch up: Real Madrid star admits he 'trained less' while on luxury yacht trip and blames Brazil's early World Cup exit - and 'overwhelming' Arsenal rumours - for sluggish start to the season

Published: 09:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:48 EST, 16 November 2026

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday after Brazil's last-16 World Cup exit is behind his slow start with Real Madrid this season.

And the winger says he felt 'overwhelmed' by the interest of clubs such as Arsenal  and insecurity around his contract renewal talks in Madrid.

He has scored one goal and provided three assists in 12 games this season, and amid the criticism, manager Jose Mourinho has even said he should have left this summer to go somewhere he is 'respected'.

Vini Jr said: 'I don’t think I prepared better after the World Cup because the impact of this tournament is very significant for all Brazilians. Losing so early was something we didn’t expect.

'So I took advantage of the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years. This may have affected my start to the season.

'Also, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs interested last summer, I felt really overwhelmed, as did the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long.

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday is behind his slow start to the season (Instagram: vinijr)

The Real Madrid star spent plenty of time relaxing on yachts as he visited Brazil, Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai (Instagram: vinijr)

The 26-year-old got around via private jet and said that he wants to 'enjoy life' (Instagram: vinijr)

'Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult. I believe only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to maintain it for so many years, achieving the same numbers.

'I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve. I try to understand more about football, about the day-to-day, but I'm 26 years old and I have to enjoy life a little too.

'Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals, as in all other seasons. I believe I am preparing, evolving, because, in the most decisive moment of the season, I am always there.'

Vini Jr spent part of his summer break in his home city of Sao Goncalo, as well as visiting Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai.

His Instagram was full of pictures of him relaxing on yachts, speeding around on a private jet, and showing off his fashionable outfits.

Arsenal enquired about the Brazilian superstar and reports suggested they were willing to offer him a mammoth £18.5million per season - more than any player at the club.

His contract expires at the end of the season and the club's position is that he must lower his demands if they are to agree an extension. They would still be willing to make him their joint-highest earner alongside Kylian Mbappe.

He has often been a target of racism in Spain - there have been more than 20 such cases of alleged abuse towards him since he joined from Flamengo in 2018. The situation has reduced him to tears before, but he has insisted on staying in La Liga so that he doesn't 'give the racists what they want'.

The winger - who has scored one goal and provided three assists this season - was a target for Arsenal and could leave Madrid in January

The winger is currently serving a four-match ban for pulling Villarreal star Nathan Saliba's hair.

And Mourinho said last month: 'If I were in his shoes, I probably wouldn't be here. I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected, but out of loyalty to Real Madrid and love for the club, he stayed.

'He believes things can improve, and he still has that smile. Nothing and no one can take it away from him.

'He's a fantastic guy, and it's easy to get along with him. I spend a few minutes alone with him every day.

'I value him immensely because he always manages to live and survive with a smile.'

Vinicius has been a phenomenon at Real Madrid, scoring 129 times in 388 games from the wing.

But the balance of power shifted to Mbappe when he joined from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 and talk of his future has increased.

There is a chance that, if Madrid go a third season in a row without significant silverware, they choose to rebuild and go in a different direction.

Moving away from the heavy 'superstar' model has worked for PSG and rewarded them with two Champions League titles in a row.

Vinicius had a tricky summer, being knocked out of the last 16 of the World Cup with Brazil and then missing his pre-season return date as his representatives tried to revive talks over a contract extension.

If an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling in January, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer for the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

#1852. Di Marzio: Endrick and Tresoldi deals ‘not a financial issue’ for Milan – the situation

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

“That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

“We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

“But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”

#1851. Aston Villa vs Sunderland - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:31

Sunderland will endeavour to claim back-to-back Premier League victories and climb out of the relegation zone when they travel to Villa Park to face Aston Villa on Saturday afternoon.

A seven-goal spectacular was witnessed when these two teams last locked horns in April, with Tammy Abraham netting a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 4-3 home triumph for Villa.

Following a strong run of six wins and one draw across seven games in all competitions, Aston Villa have failed to come out on top in any of their last four matches (D2 L2), with their latest setback sparking a furious reaction from manager Unai Emery.

Villa allowed Man United to come from two goals behind twice and salvage a point in a chaotic 4-4 draw at Old Trafford prior to the international break, with the visitors conceding two goals in stoppage time to be denied what would have been just their third win at the Theatre of Dreams in 32 visits.

Three wins, four draws and three defeats have been posted by the Midlands club in 10 top-flight games this term, leaving them sitting 10th in the Premier League table and five points behind the top four where they finished last season.

Since the beginning of October, Villa have dropped a joint-division-high six points from winning positions, while their defensive concerns remain having conceded in 13 of their 16 matches across all competitions this season.

Heading into Emery’s 150th Premier League game in charge this weekend, Villa have found the net 14 times across a five-game unbeaten home run (W3 D2), while they have lost just one of their last 12 top-flight meetings with Sunderland (W5 D6) – a 3-1 away defeat in January 2016.

Sunderland ended a miserable seven-game winless run in the Premier League with a much-needed 1-0 triumph over Chelsea at the Stadium of Light before the international break, courtesy of a first-half penalty from Enzo Le Fee.

Head coach Regis Le Bris was delighted to see his Black Cats side ‘re-connect with our identity and our fans’ after delivering a gritty and disciplined display that helped them climb off the foot of the Premier League table for the first time in three weeks.

Now sitting 19th and only three points behind Hull in 13th spot, Sunderland will be looking to win consecutive top-flight games for the first time this season when they make the trip to Villa Park this weekend, as well as end their five-game winless streak on the road.

The Black Cats sit rock bottom of the away form table having accumulated only one point (D1 L4) and conceded a joint-division-high 13 goals, including three in a 3-1 defeat at Coventry City at the end of last month.

Sunderland now head to the Midlands seeking to end a seven-game winless run away against Aston Villa across all competitions (D3 L4), with their last victory at Villa Park coming in January 2011 when Phil Bardsley’s late strike secured a 1-0 Premier League triumph under Steve Bruce.

Aston Villa's Amadou Onana – who signed a contract extension earlier this week – and Matteo Ruggeri both remain sidelined through injury, while Matty Cash is also out after picking up concussion on international duty with Poland.

However, Johan Manzambi is available for selection after recovering from a calf issue, while Aaron Wan-Bissaka should also be ready to play after missing the last six games with a thigh injury. He could therefore compete with Taylor Harwood-Bellis for the right-back berth.

Nicolas Jackson, John McGinn and Alysson were all on the scoresheet at Old Trafford and will hope to retain their starting spots in the final third. Leon Goretzka also scored against Man United but he faces competition from Joao Gomes to start in centre-midfield alongside Boubacar Kamara.

As for Sunderland, Le Bris has confirmed that captain Granit Xhaka (calf) and striker Brian Brobbey (thigh) are ruled out due to injury, joining Romaine Mundle (knee), Daniel Ballard and Habib Diarra (both thigh) in the treatment room.

However, Omar Alderete is back from a one-match suspension and could replace Luke O'Nein at centre-back, joining Trai Hume, Nordi Mukiele and Reinildo Mandava in defence.

Chemsdine Talbi was handed his first PL start of the season against Chelsea and will hope to continue on the left flank ahead of Nilson Angulo, while Wilson Isidor – who scored home and away against Villa last season – is set to lead the line in Brobbey's absence.

Suzuki; Harwood-Bellis, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Goretzka; Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi; Jackson

Roefs; Hume, Mukiele, Alderete, Reinildo; Ahoka, Sadiki; Meunier, Le Fee, Talbi; Isidor

Aston Villa's game management has become a growing concern, and Sunderland should fancy their chances of finding the net given that the hosts have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last six matches in all competitions.

While the Black Cats will be desperate to build on their victory over Chelsea as they bid to climb away from danger, the absence of both Xhaka and Brobbey is a real blow, and we expect Villa to ultimately navigate their way to a narrow triumph on home soil.

#1850. Tottenham XI vs Ipswich: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Premier League

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Tottenham are set to welcome back a host of players ahead of their Premier League clash at home to Ipswich this weekend.

Destiny Udogie, Savio, James Maddison, and Lucas Bergvall were all pictured in training at Hotspur Way this week and are now in contention for minutes on Saturday.

Udogie was left out of Roberto De Zerbi’s squad as Spurs lost 1-0 to Leeds before the international break, though the Italian left-back took to social media to suggest he was not injured.

De Zerbi has previously said that Udogie’s injuries were becoming “problematic”, with the 23-year-old starting just two league games this season.

Savio, meanwhile, is in line to return to action for the first time since October’s 1-1 draw with Manchester United. The Brazilian winger has missed Spurs’ last four league games with a muscular issue.

Spurs sorely lacked a creative threat against Leeds. But despite naming Maddison on the bench at Elland Road, De Zerbi didn't bring him on in search of a goal, raising concerns about his fitness.

Maddison has struggled to train consistently since the start of the season and came off midway through Spurs’ 2-0 win over Chelsea with a suspected groin issue.

The 29-year-old has not featured since that historic victory at Stamford Bridge, despite being available for selection. Still, it is hoped that during the international break he has had time to work on building his fitness.

Bergvall is also expected to be in contention for minutes against Ipswich, having returned from a knee injury.

The Swedish midfielder was not called up for international duty by Graham Potter, but could make his first appearance since the start of October after returning to Spurs training.

Mathys Tel is expected to be out for up to three weeks with an Achilles injury sustained following a heavy tackle from Leeds defender Jayden Bogle.

It is also unclear whether reserve goalkeeper Martin Dubravka has recovered from a knee injury, while Tosin Adarabioyo remains out with a calf issue.

Long-term absentee Xavi Simons is ahead of schedule in his recovery from an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury, but remains some time away from a return to match action.

Wilson Odobert is also out with an ACL injury, while Chelsea loanee Mykhailo Mudryk is still missing with an ankle ligament injury that has kept him out since September.

Tottenham predicted XI: Kinsky, Porro, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson, Fernandes, Tonali, Gallagher, Kudus, Solanke, Marmoush

#1849. Liverpool XI vs Manchester United: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Andoni Iraola should have a relatively healthy squad to choose from when he selects Liverpool’s starting XI to face arch-rivals Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday.

And the Basque had plenty of good news to deliver at his pre-match press conference, as he confirmed Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch. and Jeremie Frimpong - all previously considered doubts - would be fit to feature.

Both missed out on international duty with the Netherlands - van Dijk pulling out of the squad after concerns over a ‘little niggle’ he has been carrying.

Dominik Szoboszlai has struggled with fitness in recent weeks, but came through two games for Hungary unscathed. Iraola will have also have been pleased by the news that Alexander Isak was rested for Sweden’s second game of the international break, leaving the Reds’ top scorer in top condition for the weekend.

In goal, veteran Alisson will start in between the sticks. Van Dijk’s decision to drop out of the Netherlands squad seemed precautionary, and it is hoped he will feature here.

The Dutchman is building a strong connection with Jeremy Jacquet at the back. Milos Kerkez is first choice at left back, but injuries at right-back have caused Iraola headaches all season.

Ronald Araujo has deputised on the right for the majority of the season, and he will likely start there again.

A fully fit Szoboszlai is Liverpool’s best midfielder, so the Hungarian is slated to start alongside Alexis Mac Allister in the heart of the Reds’ team.

Florian Wirtz saw his best run of form since signing for the club last summer interrupted slightly by injury, but the German should soon get back into a rhythm with another start at number 10.

On the wings, Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo are emerging as first choices - but it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Victor Munoz start ahead of Barcola.

Up top, Isak will once again lead the line. The Swede will hope to add to his seven Premier League goals in nine top-flight appearances.

#1848. Blackpool vs Wigan Athletic - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 19:07, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:13

In their first game following the departure of Ian Evatt, Blackpool will welcome Wigan Athletic to Bloomfield Road on Saturday.

The hosts parted ways with their boss on Thursday and sit one place above the bottom four in the League One table and two points behind their visitors.

Blackpool return to action on Saturday fresh off the dismissal of manager Evatt with the hopes of climbing away from the League One drop zone.

They endured a tough start to their first full campaign under Evatt, currently sitting 20th with just 12 points on the board from 13 games, winning three and losing seven of those.

The most recent of those victories came in October to end a six-game winless run in the third tier, but the Tangerines failed to build on it, going on to lose 4-1 to Mansfield and rescue a 1-1 draw against a Sheffield Wednesday side who played the second half with 10 men.

Then after scraping past non-league AFC Hornchurch in extra time in the FA Cup first round, they visited AFC Wimbledon last weekend and again came away empty-handed, having failed to find a leveller after Alistair Smith's 13th-minute.

That triggered the dismissal of Evatt by the club hierarchy on Thursday, and now under the temporary charge of Steve Thompson and only above the relegation zone on goal difference, they will be desperate to begin rebuilding confidence and a cushion over the bottom four with a much-needed home win.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the short trip aiming to continue an upturn in form and their climb away from the relegation zone.

Wigan Athletic also endured a tough start to their League One campaign under Gary Caldwell, sitting bottom after 12 games with just seven points on the board having lost nine of those matches.

That was largely down to the Latics' struggles in attack, but they appear to have turned a corner since, winning two and drawing one of their last three league games while scoring five goals, firstly ending a three-game losing run by beating fellow strugglers Bromley 3-2.

Then following a stalemate with Mansfield Town and consecutive cup wins over Boreham Wood and Crewe Alexandra, Caldwell's men went into another important contest at home to Barnsley on Saturday and won 2-1 as Fraser Murray put them ahead, Cameron McGeehan pegged them back and Jensen Weir scored the decisive goal 15 minutes from time.

Still with plenty of cause for concern in their away record, having drawn one and lost six of seven league games on the road, but finally with some momentum on their side, Wigan Athletic head to Bloomfield Road in search of a third win in four games to build on their two-point lead over the drop zone.

Blackpool were hit by a sickness bug for last weekend's game, with Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe among those to miss out.

They may be back in contention for Saturday, while defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe remain sidelined alongside George Honeyman.

Karoy Anderson will head back from international duty with Jamaica but was in action in Mexico on Wednesday, while Dion Charles, Jerry Yates, CJ Hamilton and Niall Ennis will all compete for attacking places after Dale Taylor and Tom Bloxham partnered up up top last time out.

Wigan Athletic will likely remain without forwards Dara Costelloe and Luke Harris due to ongoing injuries.

Scott Hogan is back in contention after a brief layoff and came off the bench last time out, but Caldwell may go unchanged from the Barnsley win, with Christian Saydee leading the line with support from Bradley Burrowes and Jon Mellish.

Murray will continue to offer attacking support in a wing-back role after his opener against Barnsley, while Weir and Max Power will continue in the middle of a 3-4-3 setup.

Southwood; Williams, Casey, Ashworth; Niskanen, Morgan, Brown, Coulson; Bowler, Charles, Yates

Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett, Weir, Power, Murray; Burrowes, Mellish; Saydee

Blackpool remain devoid of confidence and have been hit by injuries, illness and a managerial departure, but they still have more quality than their league standing suggests while the visitors have been poor away from home this season.

We see the Tangerines at least avoiding defeat against a resurgent Wigan team.

#1847. Manchester United XI vs Liverpool: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Mauricio Pochettino will pick his first Manchester United team on Sunday for a daunting debut away at Liverpool.

The Argentine was appointed Michael Carrick’s successor last week and only arrived in the north-west on Wednesday, leaving him just a handful of sessions to prepare his side for a crunch fixture.

As such, wholesale changes from life under Carrick are not forecast, at least in terms of setup. After all, both managers have a penchant for the same 4-2-3-1 formation.

Carlos Baleba remains sidelined with a hamstring injury sustained against Roma in the Champions League, with Benjamin Sesko also out until the new year, but Pochettino may well be boosted by the returns of Marcus Rashford and Luke Shaw. The latter seems the more likely of the two, with Rashford yet to be pictured in training since the international break.

Pochettino is known to be very fond of Rashford, and has reportedly attempted to sign him to other teams he has managed, meaning he can expect to get the nod if fit.

Should fit-again Shaw slot in at left-back, he may do so as one of two fresh faces in the back four. Lisandro Martinez has served his red card suspension and will be available to partner Harry Maguire, with Diogo Dalot at right-back.

A midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo will sit behind the trio of Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Amad Diallo, with Bryan Mbeumo leading the line.

Patrick Dorgu is expected to be fit, too, but it remains to be seen whether he can unseat Matheus Cunha off the left. He could also deputise Shaw if his fitness levels are not up to par.

Leaked drone footage of United’s Thursday training session appeared to show Pochettino working on tactics with a tight-knit group of ten outfield players, leading some to speculate that he might be dealing with Sunday’s starters. The presence of Joshua Zirkzee and Harry Amass in the group rather debunks this, though, given neither has started a Premier League match this season.

Predicted Man Utd XI vs Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo

Time and date: 4.30pm GMT on Sunday, November 22

#1846. Jashari, Athekame, Camarda and Bartesaghi all start on international duty – their numbers

There were more AC Milan players in action for their national team on Monday night, with largely positive results.

Switzerland celebrated qualifying for Group A of next season’s Nations League with a resounding 4-0 victory over Scotland. Ardon Jashari and Zachary Athekame both started the game in Murat Yakin’s 3-4-2-1 system, with the former in the double pivot and the latter at right wing-back.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Jashari played the full 90 minutes and put in a solid performance. The midfielder ensured precision and order in possession, finishing the match with a 95% pass accuracy rate: 74 completed out of 78 attempted passes, plus four successful long balls out of six attempted.

Athekame remained on the pitch until the 86th minute. He recorded 42 of 44 passes completed – equal to 95% accuracy – plus four crosses, and four defensive blocks. The wing-back role gave him license to get forward, amid rumours he could return to Milan early.

A post shared by 🇨🇭Nati Men (@swissnatimen)

Meanwhile, Italy U21s were in action against Belgium. After their 2-1 victory over France in Laval, Silvio Baldini’s side made five changes to their starting line-up, but the coach still fielded Davide Bartesaghi and Francesco Camarda from the start in a 2-2 draw.

Camarda had one shot which was classed as a ‘big chance missed’ by Sofascore. He completed 10/12 passes and one was a key pass, while he had 19 touches overall and lost possession 3 times, drawing 2 fouls. The striker also chipped in with 2 clearances, 1 recovery, 2 ground duels won (out of 2) and 1 aerial duel won (out of one).

Bartesaghi meanwhile completed 2 of 7 crosses, 36/43 passes, 4/7 long balls, had 70 touches, 2 successful dribbles, lost possession 17 times, had 2 interceptions, 3 clearances, 7 recoveries, 1 blocked shot, 5 ground duels won (out of 9) and 1 aerial duel won.

#1845. Telstar vs PEC Zwolle - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:40

Matchday 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie season sees Telstar host PEC Zwolle at BUKO Stadion on Saturday evening.

Both teams begin this weekend’s clash within three points of the automatic relegation places, and neither will want to leave empty-handed.

A 10-match winless run between August 8 and October 23 dampened any optimism that may have been brewing after Telstar’s season-opening win over NEC. However, they have since responded with four points from a possible six, most recently earning a 2-2 draw against Fortuna Sittard.

Having been tipped by many as the next managerial casualty of 2026-27, Henk Brugge appears to have bought himself some breathing room, but he will know his position remains precarious, and any underwhelming result could still spell the end for him.

Averaging two goals per home league match this term, De Witte Leeuwen have found little difficulty scoring in front of their fans, although much of that good work is being undone by a porous defence that has conceded 17 times across six home games.

January’s 4-1 defeat marked Telstar’s seventh straight loss against Zwolle and extended their winless run in this fixture to 16 matches across all competitions dating back to February 2007. This weekend’s hosts will need to buck an unpleasant trend to secure all three points.

A 4-2 triumph over FC Utrecht in their most recent home match ended a run of six games without a win for Telstar, who now seek back-to-back victories in Velsen for the first time since beating Sparta Rotterdam and Heracles by a combined score of 7-1 to close out 2025-26 on a high.

After weeks of searching, PEC Zwolle will have a new face in the dugout for their upcoming clash against Telstar, with Alex Pastoor recently appointed as head coach until the end of the 2026-27 season. He replaces Henry van der Vegt, whose 15-month tenure ended in October.

Pastoor’s immediate task will be to build on his side’s four-game league unbeaten run, during which they have collected eight points from a possible 12, with only Heerenveen (12) and Ajax (10) boasting a better record in the division.

With three of their next four matches coming against teams currently in the top seven - AZ Alkmaar, Fortuna Sittard, and PSV Eindhoven - De Blauwvingers could use a win here as they look to put some distance between themselves and the drop zone before the end of 2026.

Both of Saturday’s opponents have managed just three clean sheets between them from 24 matches this season, so this weekend’s clash is likely to be decided at the attacking end. On that front, Zwolle have struggled compared to their hosts, scoring five fewer goals so far.

However, the visitors could tilt things in their favour with a quick start, and having scored the opener in four of the last five gameweeks, they may look to capitalise on a Telstar side that has conceded first four times during that span.

Gerald Alders, 21, has missed Telstar’s last four matches and will remain sidelined for Saturday’s clash as he continues his recovery to full fitness.

Rui Mendes is also unlikely to feature for the hosts, though his comeback is not far off after missing the last three matches.

Tyrone Owusu has four goals and one assist in his last six outings, already making this his most productive season in a Telstar shirt.

Deadline-day loan signing Filip Krastev has yet to feature this term due to an Achilles tendon injury sustained while playing for Goztepe.

Givaro Rahajaan and Sherel Floranus are also unavailable this weekend, but both are nearing their respective returns.

#1844. The one Crystal Palace tradition that Thomas Frank must change if former Tottenham boss is to succeed

Crystal Palace sacked Pierre Sage and hired Thomas Frank because they needed change. They need more than their new manager seems to realise.

The Dane revealed on Thursday that the 3-4-3 formation Palace have become so used to playing under Oliver Glasner and then briefly under Sage will “definitely be one of our systems, a go-to - and then we'll see what we change.”

The truth, though, is that while flexibility is good, the formation is one of the things that does need a rethink.

Frank was right about one thing, at least. “It is obvious that this squad is recruited to 3-4-3”, he said. “That's why we have very good players in their positions.”

But those “very good players” are not still at Selhurst Park. The Eagles have been persevering with a system that suits players no longer at the club, something the new boss must put right.

Wind the clock back less than a year and after a 2-1 win over London rivals Fulham, Palace sat fourth in the Premier League table in a season destined produce historic European silverware.

Adam Wharton was firing. Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta were doing well to cover up the loss of Eberechi Eze to Arsenal. Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi were two-thirds of one of the finest centre-back crews in the division. Daniel Munoz was the most enjoyable high-flying wing-back to watch in England. In charge was Glasner, a man who knew exactly how to eke out the best of Palace’s 3-4-3. Life could not get any better.

Now, it is an entirely different landscape.

Though Jaydee Canvot and Chelsea-bound Honest Ahanor are promising players, Palace also have Axel Disasi - who still has a mistake in him - and there is therefore an awful lot of pressure on the shoulders of the one central defender who lived through all the good times: Chris Richards.

In their last game, midfielder Jefferson Lerma started there while actual centre-backs sat on the bench: which is never a good sign. A 3-4-3 system involves playing one more centre-half than most teams, and yet for Palace that means one more player in a position where the quality just isn’t there anymore since Guehi and Lacroix’s departures.

In midfield, Wharton has lost his way this season and is being overrun alongside Daichi Kamada. Switching to a 4-2-3-1 - a formation Frank knows well - would allow three midfielders to get a better handle on things, provided the No10 adopted defensive responsibilities. The likelihood of such a porous Palace midfield would drop.

At wing-back, only Anan Khalaili suits a back five any more than a back four. Oscar Mingueza is the more defensively astute right-back. The pair should share game time depending on whether Palace are hunting a leveller or preserving a lead. On the other flank, Tyrick Mitchell has a claim to being the best one-v-one defender in the Premier League. Scaling him from wing-back to left-back would be no issue.

Palace must remember where they are. They sit bottom of the Premier League by a point and have the worst defence in the division.

Frank has been hired to save them, with plenty of time to do so. That means plenty of time to find a way of getting the best out of the squad as it is now, with the players available. Not getting the best out of a team that no longer exists.

#1842. Mauricio Pochettino sets out non-negotiables ahead of Man United bow at Anfield

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 19:38, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 19:39

Mauricio Pochettino has explained the importance of 'creating the culture' at Manchester United, as the Argentine looks to build a positive environment following his arrival as head coach.

The 54-year-old will take charge of his first Man United match on Sunday afternoon, when the 20-time English champions tackle Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino officially started work as Red Devils head coach on Wednesday, having flown straight to England after managing his final USA game against Haiti.

The South American has taken charge of a team that currently sit down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, picking up just eight points from their first 10 games of the season.

“It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club. Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free," Pochettino told Man United's official website.

“The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

"When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your teammates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

“That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero. I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.

“To create the culture is the most important [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create. We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.

“The best squad that we can have are the players that we have and we need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players.

"We need to provide all the tools for them to perform. It's only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the facility to translate all their talent on the field.”

Pochettino's training session on Thursday included both Harry Maguire and Patrick Dorgu, with the defensive duo both in line to be available against Liverpool.

#1839. Romelu Lukaku announces 'bombshell' international retirement: Former Chelsea star, 33, U-turns on his Belgium future - leaving Belgian press stunned

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 08:03 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:49 EST, 16 November 2026

Romelu Lukaku has announced his retirement from international football in a 'bombshell' decision that has left the Belgian press utterly stunned.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward, 33, vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team, although he now appears to have changed his mind over his future.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku took to social media on Monday morning to break the unexpected news.

'16 years old,' his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'

Belgium legend Romelu Lukaku has announced his decision to retire from international football

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking on the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retires as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

Belgian newspapers were caught out by the shock announcement, which was described as an 'unexpected bombshell' by outlet HLN on Monday.

Lukaku's stock within the international set-up has fallen since he promised the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament in January.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the tournament under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1

Axel Witsel sent a heartfelt message to Lukaku on Instagram: 'Thanks for everything, legend'

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute - and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.
