#1800. ‘I’d rather go to the Champions League than win the derbies and finish 15th’, says Pellegrini

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Real Betis boss Manuel Pellegrini revealed he "would rather go to the Champions League and not win than win the derbies and finish 15th".

Betis take on rivals Sevilla in LaLiga on Saturday, with both sides looking to make a push for the Champions League places this season.

Betis are fourth after 10 games, seven points behind leaders Barcelona following a 2-0 win over Elche before the international break.

Sevilla, meanwhile, are eight points behind their rivals in sixth ahead of their clash at Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan.

Pellegrini has won two of his last three LaLiga games against Sevilla (D1), after failing to win any of his previous 10 (D6 L4). Away from home, he has only won three of his 15 matches against Sevilla in the competition (D3 L9).

The former Manchester City boss acknowledged the importance of the rivalry, but has bigger goals in mind for his Betis side.

"I expect Sevilla to have a clear, very direct style of football, they play in their own half and will be a very dangerous team," said Pellegrini.

"The approaches are different every year because the squads are different. Rivalry is always positive as long as it stays on the pitch and not off the field. We will try again to overcome them through our style of play.

"For the fans, winning all the derbies would be important. But if I had to choose, I'd rather go to the Champions League and not win than win the derbies and finish 15th.

"The most important thing is to get the three points. The best way to win is to maintain the same style of play we showed against other opponents. Playing away from home doesn't change our fundamental approach."

— Real Betis Balompié (@RealBetis_en) November 20, 2026

Lucien Agoume has regained possession 65 times in the 2026-27 LaLiga season; only Barcelona's Pedri (69) has completed more recoveries among outfield players in the competition this term.

Marc Bartra has scored three goals in eight LaLiga games this season; only Atletico Madrid's Alejandro Grimaldo (four) has scored more among all defenders in the competition this term.

Sevilla have lost two of their last three LaLiga matches against Betis (D1) after not losing any of their previous 12 against them in the competition (W7 D5).

Sevilla have also picked up points in 11 of their last 13 home LaLiga games against Betis (W9 D2 L2), although they lost the most recent meeting 2-0 in November 2025.

Betis are unbeaten in their last four away LaLiga matches (W2 D2), keeping clean sheets in their last two. They have not recorded three consecutive away clean sheets in the competition since October 2022 (W1 D2).

Sevilla have won just one of their last five LaLiga derbies against Andalusian teams (D1 L3). Betis, however, have lost only one of their last 14 derbies in the competition (W6 D7), but that defeat was against Sevilla (1-0 in October 2024).

Sevilla boss Luis Garcia has faced Pellegrini 11 times in LaLiga, more than any other coach (P11 W2 D4 L5), failing to win any of his last six meetings with him (D4 L2).

#1799. Bradford City vs Doncaster Rovers - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:09

Bradford City and Doncaster Rovers will square off on Saturday in a Yorkshire derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.

The hosts sit a point outside of the playoff places following a defeat last time out while their visitors have dropped into the bottom four due to consecutive losses.

Bradford City head into their first League One game of November at the weekend following an international break with the hopes of returning to winning ways and moving back into the top six.

After winning promotion from League Two and losing in the League One playoffs in the last two seasons, the Bantams picked up where they left off in early 2026-27, winning five of their first seven outings before Graham Alexander departed for Preston North End.

They then turned to Michael Duff and have struggled to continue their hot start since, winning one, drawing four and losing one of their last six league matches with the only victory coming against Stevenage in mid-October.

That did form part of a run of four straight clean sheets for the Bantams, who top the division with nine and have conceded a league-low tally of eight goals, but that came to an end in their last league outing against fellow promotion-chasers and Yorkshire rivals Huddersfield Town, who dished out a 3-0 beating at Mbanq Valley Parade.

Now, at least, on the back of a pair of confidence-boosting cup wins before their break, beating Marine 7-0 in the FA Cup and York City 4-0 in the EFL Trophy, Bradford City now sit eighth, but just two points off fourth spot, and will hope to retake a top-six spot and kickstart another hot streak in League One.

Their visitors, meanwhile, make the trip across Yorkshire in search of a return to winning ways of their own in their battle at the other end of League One.

Doncaster Rovers also won promotion from League Two in 2024-25 and finished 14th last time around on their return to the second tier but now find themselves 21st with just 12 points on the board from 13 games.

That is in no small part down to a poor away record, having lost five of seven games on the road, collected just four points and conceded 16 goals in those.

Two heavy away defeats have come consecutively for Grant McCann's side since a home victory over Sheffield Wednesday, as they lost 3-1 at Luton Town and 6-1 in their last third-tier match away at MK Dons at the end of October.

Having also since played two cup games, beating Rochdale in the EFL Trophy and losing 3-0 away at non-league Kidderminster Harriers in the FA Cup, Doncaster Rovers now head into a tough trip aiming to kickstart an upturn in form in League One and climb out of the bottom four.

Doncaster Rovers form (all competitions):

Bradford City remain without wide men Josh Neufville and Tyreik Wright, while attacker Bobby Pointon also missed their last outing through injury.

Corey O'Keeffe will continue in a wing-back role in Neufville's absence, while Antoni Sarcevic will start in midfield having served a suspension in the FA Cup for a red card received in their last league game.

George Lapslie, Adam Phillips and Nick Powell will all compete for starts in attack after Jake Beesley led the line with support from Kayden Jackson and Will Swan in the 3-0 defeat to Huddersfield.

Doncaster Rovers continue to contend with several injury issues, as James Collins, Francis Okoronkwo, Matty Pearson, James Husband and Tommy O'Reilly should all remain sidelined.

McCann made some rotations in their two cup games and should make changes from the team that lost 6-1 to MK Dons in their last league outing, with the likes of Robbie Gotts and Will Keane pushing to start after being reduced to substitute appearances.

Hakeeb Adelakun will also challenge for a start on the wing and may join Isaac Hutchinson and Jordan Thomas in support of a lone striker unless captain and key man Owen Bailey returns to an advanced midfield role.

McCracken; Pennington, Baldwin, Pratt; O'Keeffe, Sarcevic, Connolly, Touray; Swan, Beesley, Phillips

Doncaster Rovers possible starting lineup:

Simkin; Sterry, Grehan, Byrne, Senior; Broadbent, Gotts; Thomas, Bailey, Adelakun; Keane

Bradford City have certainly not been at their best in League One since Michael Duff's arrival, but still boasting the league's standout defensive record, and having rebuilt confidence with a pair of dominant cup wins, we back them to come out on top at home to a struggling Doncaster team.

#1797. Feyenoord vs SBV Excelsior - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:13

Feyenoord host SBV Excelsior at Stadion Feijenoord (De Kuip) in Rotterdam in round 13 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie on Saturday.

The Pride of South sit second in the Eredivisie table on 25 points, one behind PSV after losing 5-3 at Heerenveen on November 8, while Excelsior are 15th on 11 points, one clear of the relegation play-off place after five straight league defeats.

Giovanni van Bronckhorst's side arrive without a win in five matches in all competitions, having lost 1-0 at Real Betis on October 21, drawn 1-1 with PSV and Fortuna Sittard, lost 3-0 at home to Inter Milan on November 3 and lost 5-3 at Heerenveen.

Heerenveen was Feyenoord's first league defeat of the season, and it came after they led 2-0 through Anis Hadj Moussa and a Nacho Ferri penalty, only for substitute Ringo Meerveld to score a hat-trick.

Their attack has not been the problem, as 36 league goals in 12 games trail only PSV's 40, and a 5-0 home win over Utrecht on September 20 featured two goals from Hadj Moussa plus strikes from Ferri, Luciano Valente and Gaoussou Diarra.

The damage is coming at the other end, where Feyenoord have conceded seven goals in their last three league games after allowing 10 in the first nine, and they have let in at least one in each of their last five matches in all competitions.

Goalkeeper Tjark Ernst, signed from Hertha BSC for €5m in the summer, received sarcastic applause from home supporters after a routine catch against Inter, and Opta figures published by NOS rate only two Eredivisie goalkeepers worse than him at keeping out shots, although Van Bronckhorst continues to select him.

Captain Valente said after the Heerenveen defeat that things clearly had to change, while Van Bronckhorst has said that opponents have adapted to the way Feyenoord play.

Ruben den Uil's side won 4-0 at Cambuur in their opening game to go top of the Eredivisie for the first time in 47 years, and they had 10 points from five games after a draw at NEC on September 8.

Since then Excelsior have taken one point from a possible 21, a run of seven games that includes a 2-2 draw at Ajax on September 19 despite being outshot 33-8, a 1-5 home loss to Groningen and a 4-0 defeat at Heerenveen on October 16.

In their last five league games, Excelsior have conceded 20 goals and scored once, a stretch that includes a 9-0 defeat by Twente on November 1, the heaviest in the club's league history, in which Nesto Groen was sent off after five minutes for a challenge on Robin Propper.

Go Ahead Eagles then won 1-0 at Excelsior on November 7 through Soren Tengstedt, in a game Den Uil described as a typical 0-0, which left the Kralingers without a goal in four league games and on 16 for the season, four of which came in the opening win at Cambuur.

Aymen Sliti, who has three league goals, and defender Jan Plug are both on loan from Feyenoord, and Sliti has said he will not celebrate if he scores at De Kuip.

Feyenoord have eased the restrictions on visiting supporters for the derby, who will not be required to use organised transport to De Kuip.

Hadj Moussa is a major doubt after a sprained ankle on international duty with Algeria following the game against Togo, and Feyenoord-watcher Martijn Krabbendam said on Voetbal International's podcast that reaching the derby will be difficult, with the club aiming to have him ready for the Klassieker against Ajax on November 29, although Kicker reported that he left the Algeria camp after a dispute with the coach rather than through injury.

Jeremiah St. Juste is still out with a shin problem and Van Bronckhorst hopes to have him back before the winter break, while Bart Nieuwkoop, Jordan Bos and Thomas Beelen are not expected until after it and Tijme Wessels is recovering from knee surgery.

Reiss Nelson and Shaqueel van Persie are available again after injuries, Gijs Smal has returned to group training and Jakub Moder, who has played one minute this season, is also being eased back, although neither is certain for Saturday and no Feyenoord player is suspended.

For the visitors, Groen misses the derby serving the last game of a three-match ban, with one match suspended, for the red card against Twente, which leaves Mario Dominguez or David Garden to lead the line.

Sliti hurt his hand in the Netherlands Under-21s' 3-2 defeat by Denmark on November 17 and fears a bruised or broken thumb, but he has said he expects to play on Saturday, with former Feyenoord winger Alireza Jahanbakhsh the alternative on the flank.

Ernst; Read, Watanabe, Marmol, Lopez; Zechiel, Vanhoutte, Targhalline; Van Persie, Ferri, Valente

Van Gassel; Bos, Plug, Widell, Meissen; Yegoian, Hartjes; Naujoks, Thorsteinsson, Sliti; Dominguez

Feyenoord have won each of their last six meetings with Excelsior, scoring at least twice every time, including 2-1 wins on August 16, 2025 and March 15, 2026, and Excelsior have not won at De Kuip since 1980.

That record matters because this Excelsior side has conceded 20 goals in five league games, has lost Groen up front and faces an attack that has scored 36 times in 12 league games.

Feyenoord's own defence, which has conceded in five straight matches, and the possible absence of Hadj Moussa leave a small opening, but Excelsior have failed to score in each of their last four league games, so we expect Van Bronckhorst's side to win without needing to rely on one player.

#1796. Martinez insists Leverkusen must be ‘strong at the back’ against Paderborn

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Carles Martinez insisted his Bayer Leverkusen side must be "strong at the back" if they are to defeat Paderborn on Saturday.

Leverkusen have lost two of their last three Bundesliga matches, but defeated Koln 2-1 before the international break.

The Werkself lost 4-2 at home to Stuttgart following a 3-0 defeat at Hoffenheim, leaving Leverkusen fifth in the Bundesliga, five points behind Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund.

Paderborn, meanwhile, are 13th in the league after nine games, three points clear of the relegation playoff places, but also just six points behind Leverkusen.

Paderborn (W1 D3) are one of only three teams, alongside Bayern and Dortmund, to remain unbeaten in their last four Bundesliga matches.

This four-game unbeaten run equals Paderborn's club record in the Bundesliga, previously achieved only in their first four matches in the competition in 2014.

Martinez is wary of the task ahead in Paderborn, but hopes his Leverkusen players will perform in front of their home fans following the international break.

"The changes to the international break schedule are new for everyone," Martinez said.

"We've adapted well. After those gruelling weeks, we've used the time to recover and think carefully about exactly where and how we can improve.

"We can't wait to experience that special [home] atmosphere again – we've really missed it.

"Paderborn are having a good season, have a clear identity and try to dictate the play themselves. That's why we need to be particularly strong at the back. I expect the best from us."

GTA AND B04 BOTH BACK IN THE SAME WEEK!  https://t.co/3D9mcqauMV

— Bayer 04 Leverkusen (@bayer04_en) November 20, 2026

Patrik Schick has scored eight goals in the Bundesliga this season, finding the net in all four of his home appearances.

Eight goals after nine Bundesliga matchdays equals the club record for Leverkusen, previously achieved only by Schick himself (2021-22) and Patrick Helmes (2008-09).

The Czech forward has now scored as many league goals on his own as the entire Paderborn team.

Santiago Castaneda is the only Paderborn outfield player to have played every minute in the Bundesliga this season.

The American has also recorded the second-most interceptions in the league (25, Kaishu Sano: 27) and has covered the second-most distance (108.4 km, Hennes Behrens: 109.2 km).

Leverkusen have not lost any of their seven previous professional meetings with Paderborn in all competitions (W6 D1), winning each of the last six.

Against no other current Bundesliga side have Leverkusen played as many professional matches without suffering a single defeat.

Leverkusen lost 3-2 away to Elversberg on the opening matchday of the Bundesliga season and could now lose consecutive Bundesliga games against promoted sides for the first time since 2017.

However, the Werkself are unbeaten in their last 10 home Bundesliga matches against promoted teams (W7 D3).

Paderborn are one of three teams without an away win in the Bundesliga this season, alongside Koln and Union Berlin.

Paderborn have drawn three of those matches (L1), including two 0-0 draws, and have conceded only five away goals – only Dortmund have conceded fewer on the road (four).

#1795. Romano: Balde expected to leave Barcelona – Milan’s position after summer talks

AC Milan have been linked with a move for Alejandro Balde, but Fabrizio Romano claims some flexibility is needed from Barcelona.

In the past couple of weeks there has been more talk about Milan strengthening in the left-back role. Pervis Estupinan has not been convincing since his arrival, while Davide Bartesaghi and Diego Moreira have been used further forward in recent weeks.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yunus Musah was even adapted to playing as a left-sided defender in the recent win over Genoa, so it’s clear that Ruben Amorim might welcome a more natural player for the role, one that fits his ideas of how to play.

In a video on his YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano touched upon a number of different topics connected to Milan, from Francesco Camarda’s fate to the possibility of a young midfielder arriving. He also spoke about Balde – another recent link – and his words are via MilanNews.

“Balde is a name that can be a key player in January. Then, to be completely honest, he’s a foreign transfer name, being realistic. He earns more than €5 million net per season,” he began.

“Barcelona were willing to let him go in the summer, but wanted a permanent deal worth €50-55 million. As for Italy, despite Mendes also trying to see if there was any room for negotiation with Milan, there were never any real negotiations. Also because the costs are decidedly high.

“Balde still isn’t playing and will speak with Mendes today, who is on a mission to Barcelona to meet with the player and his family and figure out what to do in the January transfer window.

“I’d keep an eye on the possibility if the formula were to change, because these are currently foreign figures. But he’s a player to keep an eye on. We’ll see if he goes to Italy or abroad.”

#1794. Groningen vs Heerenveen - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 19 Nov 2026 23:31

FC Groningen host SC Heerenveen in the Eredivisie at Euroborg on Saturday, November 21 in the first Derby of the North of the 2026-27 season.

Sixth-placed Heerenveen arrive on 21 points on the Eredivisie table after four consecutive league wins, while ninth-placed Groningen have taken one point from their last four games and will be without their head coach, goalkeeper and first-choice right-back.

Groningen have collected one point from their last four Eredivisie matches, a run that began with a 2-5 home defeat to Ajax on October 18 and included a 2-2 draw at NEC Nijmegen.

Those four games have cost 14 goals, and the 2-3 home loss to Sparta Rotterdam on November 1 came after Jacob Ondrejka scored after 17 seconds, before a miscommunication between Etienne Vaessen and Hans Hateboer handed Andrej Kostic the winner in the 85th minute.

The latest setback came at AZ on November 8, where De Trots van het Noorden led 3-1 after 54 minutes, lost 4-3 to a Mexx Meerdink penalty in the 91st minute and finished with nine men after Vaessen collected a second yellow card for protesting the penalty and Hateboer was sent off in the 10th minute of stoppage time for a deliberate handball.

Euroborg has offered little protection this season, with Groningen winning two, drawing one and losing three of their six home league games, and a 2-0 home defeat to Dick Lukkien’s former club FC Emmen ended their KNVB Cup run in the first round on October 29.

The recent derby record still favours the hosts, who won 2-1 at Euroborg on August 16, 2025 through a stoppage-time Brynjolfur Darri Willumsson goal and 2-0 at Abe Lenstra Stadion on January 18, 2026, when captain Thijmen Blokzijl scored the second.

The off-field story is Lukkien, who had a hip replacement last week and said the derby arrived “just too early” for his recovery, so assistant Casper Goedkoop will coach from the touchline.

Heerenveen have won four consecutive league games since a 2-0 defeat at PSV Eindhoven, beating Excelsior 4-0, ADO Den Haag 3-2, NEC Nijmegen 1-0 and Feyenoord 5-3.

Those wins have brought 13 goals and five conceded, including two from Jacob Trenskow at ADO on October 24, and have lifted De Superfriezen to 21 points from 12 games with a goal difference of +8.

The 5-3 win over Feyenoord on November 8 ended the unbeaten league record of the Eredivisie leaders, with Heerenveen recovering from 2-0 down after 31 minutes through Maas Willemsen, Levi Smans and a late Ringo Meerveld hat-trick.

Meerveld came on at half time for Maxence Rivera and scored in the 61st, 84th and 93rd minutes, with Trenskow providing the pass for the first of them.

Away from Abe Lenstra Stadion, Robin Veldman’s side have won two, drawn two and lost one of their five league trips, but they have not won in Groningen since a 2-0 victory on March 19, 2023.

Veldman said after the Feyenoord game that his players wanted to extend the run, and a win would take them further clear of seventh-placed Fortuna Sittard, who sit on 20 points.

Vaessen and Hateboer are both suspended after their red cards at AZ, so Lovro Stubljar, who has been on the bench in recent league games, is expected to start in goal and Wouter Prins should move in at right-back.

Malcolm Jeng remains out with an Achilles tendon injury and goalkeeper Rijk Janse is also sidelined, while Travis Hernes and Ryan Metu are doubtful after several weeks out.

Heerenveen have no reported injuries or suspensions, so Veldman has a full squad to choose from.

Meerveld is expected to push Rivera for a start on the left of the attacking three after his hat-trick off the bench.

Stubljar; Prins, Blokzijl, Rente, Csinger; De Jonge, Clement; Schreuders, Van Bergen, Ondrejka; Willumsson

Klaverboer; Braude, Kersten, Willemsen, Zagaritis; Linday, Courtens; Trenskow, Smans, Meerveld; Vente

Heerenveen have scored 13 goals in their last four league games and have already shown they can recover from a two-goal deficit, while Groningen have conceded at least two goals in each of their last four and lose both Vaessen and Hateboer from the back line.

Groningen have won the last two derbies and have scored at least twice in each of their last four games, so Heerenveen will concede, and the crowd will matter with Lukkien watching from home.

The gap is in defensive organisation rather than attacking quality, and a Heerenveen side with a full squad and a 13-5 goal record over four wins should edge a high-scoring derby by one goal.

#1793. Chicago Fire vs Charlotte FC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 19 Nov 2026 23:33

Seeking their first-ever away victory in the MLS Cup playoffs, Charlotte FC will visit SeatGeek Stadium on Sunday for game one of their best-of-three series with the Chicago Fire.

The Fire finished fourth in the Eastern Conference this year, losing their last outing 4-3 to the Columbus Crew as they wound up a point above Charlotte, who drew 3-3 with Inter Miami on Decision Day.

Throughout 2026, Chicago were out to prove that last year was no fluke as they continued to improve in the league yet again.

In his second year as head coach, Gregg Berhalter saw his team gain two more points than in his inaugural campaign, while finishing four places higher in the Eastern Conference table this time around and making the playoffs on successive occasions.

The next step will be for the Fire to find some playoff success, with this club aiming to advance beyond the first round for the first time since 2009.

During this regular season campaign, they won three more home matches when compared to 2025, though they have only won one playoff fixture in Illinois since 2009, defeating Orlando City 3-1 in the Wildcard Round a year ago.

They have points in three of their last four MLS encounters but will try to snap a two-match domestic losing run at home this weekend, conceding a combined seven goals in those two defeats.

On Sunday, the Fire can beat Charlotte at home for a third consecutive occasion, having won those last two contests by a single goal.

The Crown are back in the post-season for a third successive occasion, hoping to get past round one at long last.

Dean Smith’s men set a single-season club record for goals scored in 2026 (66), averaging just under two per match (1.9) in the league this year.

This weekend, they will hope to end a four-match domestic winless run away from home and collect their first-ever road triumph in the post-season.

Defensively, they have been shaky as the visitors in 2026, conceding three or more goals on eight occasions in the regular season.

In round one of the playoffs, they have netted just one goal overall and have never scored in the opening half of an MLS road playoff game.

Charlotte have also never won a post-season game in normal time, and have scored first only once, in 2024 when they lost to Orlando City on penalties in the decisive third game of that best-of-three opening round series.

Due to a knock, Inter Miami loanee Noah Allen is questionable for the Fire, as is Robin Lod, who has a leg injury.

Robert Lewandowski has three goals in his last two games, netting a brace in their defeat to the Crew, with Maren Haile-Selassie also scoring on Decision Day.

On the Charlotte side, Tim Ream is questionable as he recovers from an adductor issue, Archie Goodwin may not be available due to a foot problem, Nimfasha Berchimas is recovering from foot surgery and Aron John is dealing with a shoulder injury.

Liel Abada notched a pair of goals in their regular-season finale, while a 90th-minute strike from Rodolfo Aloko earned them a point against the reigning MLS Cup champions.

Brady; Dean, Hanche-Olsen, Elliott, Gutman; Saletros, D’Avilla, Haile-Selassie; Zinckernagel, Lewandowski, Bamba

Kahlina; Byrne, Agyemang, Kessler, Toffolo; Diani, Westwood, Biel; De La Torre, Toklomati, Saint-Maximin

Big players elevate their games in big moments, and Lewandowski has usually been a difference-maker at club level, we believe his consistency and lethal finishing will prove decisive on Sunday.

#1792. OLIVER HOLT: Why England CAN now end 62 years of hurt - Thomas Tuchel is intoxicating and I'd tip Jude Bellingham to beat Kylian Mbappe to the next Ballon d'Or... plus my top 10 Three Lions performances

Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026

The glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning. ‘Fin a la racha,’ the headline said. The end of the run.

For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.

For England, the feeling was very different. Because Sunday night in the cauldron of the Metropolitano felt very much like a beginning. Thomas Tuchel has been the head coach for almost two years but this was the moment of his true arrival.

This was the victory that freed us from looking back to the Groundhog Day pain of that World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in Atlanta last summer and allowed us to look forward to a future that seems luminous and full of hope.

This was the victory that allowed us to stop blaming Tuchel for what happened four months ago and start looking forwards again, dreaming about the glories that he might yet deliver. This was the victory that validated Tuchel and why the FA hired him in the first place. This was the victory that allowed us to believe he might be the Messiah after all.

This felt like the moment when he embraced us, with all our quirks and football idiosyncrasies, and we embraced him. He had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it with bells on. Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game and welded it to his principles and the result is intoxicating.

Thomas Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game to down world champions Spain

Once you have seen England play the way they did for an hour against Spain, you are lost. You are lost to the belief that the 62 years of hurt might really be coming to an end at Wembley in the final of the European Championship in the summer of 2028. You are lost to the idea that, finally, everything is falling into place.

For the 63 minutes up until the sending off of Elliot Anderson, I have never seen an England performance as good as the one that unfolded in the Metropolitano. Spain are the best team in the world and England outclassed them and stupefied them. They were better than them with the ball and better than them without the ball. They were magnificent.

Because of the context, because of the wonder of the stage, because of the odds they faced, England’s victory over Mexico in the grandeur and the mayhem of the mighty Azteca Stadium during the World Cup might edge Sunday’s performance but for pure football, what England delivered in Madrid demands comparison with the best they have played for many a year.

This year’s World Cup came just too soon but now Tuchel and England understand each other perfectly. And now England are purring. They have a manager who commands the players’ respect and they have a group of players that commands the respect of the manager.

Yes, it was just a Nations League group game but it was against one of the best national sides the world has ever seen. England worked so ferociously and attacked so fluently and defended so devotedly that they reached a level that drew admiration even from their opponents.

Many, many things will live long in the memory. James Trafford’s miraculous double save in the dying minutes gets better every time I watch it. Ben White’s goal channels the beauty of Carlos Alberto’s strike for Brazil against Italy in the 1970 World Cup Final, too. Let’s hope that strike, and his superb defensive performance, bring an end to the boos that have been his companion of late.

Jude Bellingham was relentless, tireless and glided through the game against Spain

Tuchel had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it

And then there was Jude Bellingham. Just when you think you can’t admire him any more than you do, he delivers a performance like the one he produced against Spain, a performance that lifted him above even the exalted company of the other players on two fine teams.

Bellingham was tireless. He was relentless. He glided past challenges. He thundered into tackles. He dominated midfield. He has the heart and the sheer brilliant indomitability that Bryan Robson possessed.

Bellingham has it in him to be England’s greatest ever player. He needs trophies to fulfil that destiny but maybe, finally, trophies are in reach again.

He has the team around him to do it, which Robson never quite had. Jordan Pickford is a good goalkeeper but Trafford might just be better. Ezri Konsa had his best game for England in Spain. White and Lewis Hall were superb at full back. Little more needs to be said about England’s front six. They are as good as any unit in world football.

Harry Kane, of course, was the best player in the world last year. Some seem to assume that the Ballon d’Or will inevitably pass to Yamal or Kylian Mbappe next. I think it is more likely to be Bellingham.

The man is a colossus. He is a footballer who has everything. He does not know how to be beaten.

Bellingham saw off Barcelona rival Lamine Yamal - and could beat him to the Ballon d'Or

With them together, the sky is the limit. And Bellingham has also proved to be a player of immense mental strength. It was not so long ago that people worried about his discipline but the fortitude he showed when he was being targeted by Argentina at the World Cup was the best answer to that.

He and Kane are England’s axis of ambition on the pitch. Tuchel is lucky to have them and they are lucky to have him, too. The coach has reached the point where his tactics and his team-building are bearing fruit.

Now England have a team-manager package that genuinely need fear nobody. The victory against Spain was a rehearsal for the bigger stage of major tournaments. Going down to 10 men after 63 minutes against the best team in the world might not have been in the script but that is what rehearsals are for.

After Sunday night in the Metropolitano, England are ready for their close-up.

#1791. Luis Enrique relishing busy PSG schedule before 2027

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Luis Enrique revealed both he and his Paris Saint-Germain players are relishing their busy schedule ahead of the New Year.

After a shaky start to the season, PSG have won their last 11 matches in all competitions, the longest current run among teams in Europe's big-five leagues.

PSG sit top of Ligue 1, two points ahead of Lille, while they also lead the league phase of the Champions League after four wins in as many games.

Luis Enrique's side have four league games ahead of January, starting with a trip to Nice on Saturday, along with Champions League clashes against Roma and Aston Villa.

PSG will also take part in the Intercontinental Cup next month, and a Coupe de France match is also set to be scheduled in their calendar.

"We're looking at the coming weeks as a whole but there are lots of factors that come up on a day-to-day basis, and we need to be able to adapt," said Luis Enrique.

"We've got lots of great matches coming up before the end of the year, across several competitions, including Ligue 1, the Coupe de France, the Champions League and the Intercontinental Cup.

"We can't wait – all the players want to play and are ready to do so.

"Nice are a team in good form, winning lots of matches and unbeaten at home, with a manager who’s doing well and who’s done a good job at Lorient in recent years.

"It's always difficult to play away from home, especially after an international break, but all of that is extra motivation."

— Paris Saint-Germain (@PSG_English) November 19, 2026

Nice are sixth in Ligue 1, six points behind leaders PSG after winning each of their last three league games.

Jonathan Clauss is set to play his 200th Ligue 1 match (70 with Lens, 61 with Marseille, 68 currently with Nice).

He is the only defender to have been involved in 50 or more goals in the top-flight in the last 20 years, with 20 goals and 45 assists.

Four of PSG's last five Ligue 1 goals have been scored by defenders (three for Achraf Hakimi, one for Illia Zabarnyi).

In total, nine of PSG's goals have been scored by defenders, more than any other team in Europe's big-five leagues in the 2026-27 season.

MATCH PREDICTION: PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN WIN

Nice have failed to score in their last two Ligue 1 matches against PSG, but they have never gone three consecutive games without a goal against the Parisian club.

Nice have won five of their last six Ligue 1 matches (L1), as many victories as in their previous 34 games (D13 L16). They could record four consecutive wins in the competition for the first time since February and March 2025 (four).

PSG have scored in each of their last 23 away games in all competitions. They have scored at least three goals in each of their last four away matches (18 goals), their best such run since between April and September 2022 (nine).

Nice (seven points) and PSG (eight points) are the two teams who have gained the most points after conceding the opening goal in Ligue 1 this season.

PSG have never lost after conceding first in 2026-27 (W2 D2), while they lost all five matches in which they went 1-0 down in Ligue 1 in 2025-26.

In the UEFA Nations League match between France and Turkey on Sunday night, Maignan left the pitch at halftime with an adductor problem resulting from a collision with an opponent, which obviously sparked worries among fans and the Milan medical staff.

Yesterday, L’Equipe reported that initial tests had suggested the goalkeeper was in fine shape, and the tests conducted with the staff confirmed the initial findings. The goalkeeper has not suffered any muscular injuries and will be available for Sunday’s resumption of Serie A action.

It is a relief for Amorim, who will have his captain between the posts for the game against a side that are sixth in the table and scoring plenty of goals. Lorenzo Torriani was ready to step in again had Maignan not been able to start, but the doubts seem to have been resolved.

#1789. Sheffield United vs Watford - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:37

Aiming to break into the top eight of the Championship table on their return from the November international break, Sheffield United will welcome Watford to Bramall Lane on Saturday.

The hosts lost in their final game before the break but sit just two points outside of the playoff spots, while their visitors sit five points above the drop zone thanks to a win and a draw in their last two outings.

Sheffield United head back into Championship action after the international break on Saturday aiming to reignite their pursuit of the playoff places.

Aiming to kick on from a 13th-placed finish in 2025-26 and challenge for a return to the Premier League, the Blades experienced a mixed start to the season but looked to have turned a corner after the September and October break.

The Blades managed four wins and one draw in their first six games back from that break, scoring 11 goals and conceding six in those games, culminating in a 1-0 home victory over Wrexham, with Ben Brereton Diaz on the scoresheet, and a 3-2 away victory against Preston North End thanks to Sydie Peck's hat-trick.

They were unable to carry that winning streak into the latest break, though, visiting Charlton Athletic last time out and losing 2-1, having fallen behind and levelled through Jordan Ayew before Matt Godden scored the winner for their hosts 10 minutes from time.

Now sat 10th but just two points behind seventh and eighth spots, Sheffield United will again hope to come back firing and return to winning ways at Bramall Lane on Saturday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to South Yorkshire aiming to build on a positive turn in form before the break.

After a 16th-placed Championship finish in 2025-26 and the summer appointment of Alessio Dionisi, Watford endured a poor start to the new campaign, picking up just 11 points from their first 13 matches, winning three and losing eight of those.

The Hornets' away record is a real cause for concern, having lost six and drawn one of their seven league matches on the road, scoring just four goals in those and conceding 14.

The most recent of those was a 3-2 away loss against Norwich City, in which they led 2-0 at the break, but Dionisi's men did bounce back, beating Lincoln City 1-0 at home thanks to Stephy Mavididi's goal, before they hosted then-leaders Middlesbrough last time out and stood strong for a point from a 0-0 draw.

Watford now return to action hoping to add to those positive results and extend their five-point lead over the relegation zone.

Sheffield Wednesday are unable to call on defender Femi Seriki, who sustained a long-term injury before the break, while Matt Doherty, Ryan One and Joe Rothwell may also remain sidelined.

Patrick Bamford may be in line for a return, though, having been out with a shoulder injury, and if deemed fit he could return up front from the start despite competition for those places from Ben Brereton Diaz, Tom Cannon, Jordan Ayew and Tyrese Campbell.

Kalvin Phillips has impressed in his second loan spell with the Blades thus far and will again join Sydie Peck in midfield.

Watford are still without Kwadwo Baah, Jeremy Ngakia, Soumaila Coulibaly and Edoardo Bove on Saturday due to ongoing injuries.

Kevin Keben and Branimir Mlacic should again join Mattie Pollock in the middle of the defence after their clean sheet against Middlesbrough last time out, while Krepin Diatta may start in a wing-back role if he is fit after being forced off in that game.

Competition for attacking spots is rife with Mamadou Doumbia, Amin Nabizada, Stephy Mavididi, Luca Kjerrumgaard, Rocco Vata and Othmane Maamma all pushing to start, while Myron Boadu has often led the line but missed the Middlesbrough game.

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:

Cooper; Choudhury, Tanganga, Kitching, Burrows; Donovan, Peck, Phillips, Brereton Diaz; Cannon, Bamford

Watford showed signs of improvement before the break with consecutive clean sheets, but we fancy Sheffield United, rested after a disappointing defeat halted their notable improvement, to bounce back at Bramall Lane.

By Ben Sully | 19 Nov 2026 23:48, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 01:22

AFC Wimbledon will be looking to claim a second straight win when they make the short trip to Brisbane Road for Saturday's League One clash against Leyton Orient.

The O's, meanwhile, are bidding to record a fourth consecutive home victory in all competitions.

Leyton Orient head into the weekend in 14th spot in the League One table after recording five wins, two draws and six defeats in their 13 league games this term.

Orient cruised to a 3-0 victory in their most recent league outing against Cambridge United at the end of October, a result that has formed part of a three-game winning run on home turf.

Their last victory at Brisbane Road took place in the FA Cup first round, which saw Idris El Mizouni net a brace in an emphatic 5-1 win over sixth-tier Harborough Town to set up a second-round tie against Port Vale.

However, Richie Wellens's side were unable to repeat that sort of success in their away clash against Barnet in the EFL Trophy, falling to a 4-2 defeat as they finished at the bottom of Group F and behind third-place Wimbledon on goal difference.

Orient will now return to the familiar surroundings of Brisbane Road, where they have won four of their last five outings, including three victories without conceding in their previous four home league games.

That represents a significant improvement from the start of the season when they lost each of their opening three home matches in the third tier.

Wimbledon have played a game more than Orient, but they are a point worse off after winning four, drawing four and losing six of their 14 League One matches.

In fact, the Dons have lost four of their previous six games in the third tier, although they did manage to end an 11-game winless run in all competitions in their most recent outing against Blackpool.

Alistair Smith's first-half proved enough to fire Wimbledon to a 1-0 victory, representing their first three-point haul since recording back-to-back wins against Bromley and Doncaster Rovers in September.

After enjoying success at Plough Lane, Johnnie Jackson's side will now make the trip to Brisbane Road for the second time this season after playing out a 1-1 draw in August's EFL Trophy encounter.

They missed out on a bonus point with a defeat in the subsequent penalty shootout, but they enjoyed greater success in January's league visit, when they fought back from a goal down to claim a 3-1 victory.

However, their hopes of repeating that success may be tempered by the fact they have lost six of their last eight competitive away games, including each of their last four.

Orient midfielder Ollie O’Neill will be out for around four months after undergoing an operation not long after returning from a long injury absence.

The hosts are also expected to be without the services of Nicholas Oyekunle, Demetri Mitchell and Sean Clare.

Rarmani Edmonds-Green will feature alongside Alfie Gilchrist in central defence after returning from injury to start the wins over Cambridge and Harborough.

As for the visitors, Wimbledon are unable to call upon Josef Bursik, Dan Sweeney, Dujuan Richards, Ryan Johnson and Donnell McNeilly due to injury.

Jayden Stockley will serve a one-match ban after being sent off for two bookable offences in the narrow win over Blackpool.

Aaron Sasu could move forward to replace Stockley in the frontline, which would open the door for Steven Sessegnon to feature at left wing-back.

Baxter; Stevens, Edmonds-Green, Gilchrist, Boniface; El Mizouni, Gilbert; Connolly, Wellens, Dobra; Kabia

Bishop; Tilley, Yiadom, Ogundere, Seddon, Sessegnon; Smith, Harrison, Maycock; Cornick, Sasu

Leyton Orient have made Brisbane Road a fortress in recent times, and considering Wimbledon have lost five of their seven away league games this season, we think the signs point to a home win on Saturday.

#1786. Burton Albion vs Luton Town - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 19 Nov 2026 23:48

On their return to league action after a weekend off for the international break, Luton Town will head to the Pirelli Stadium to take on Burton Albion on Saturday.

The visitors sit five points outside of the top two in the League One table in the midst of a seven-game unbeaten streak in all competitions while their hosts are 15th after consecutive league defeats.

Burton Albion head into the weekend aiming to bounce back from a pair of defeats and move back towards the top half of League One.

Aiming to build on a 17th-placed finish last time around, the Brewers enjoyed a positive start to the new term, earning 17 points from their first 13 outings courtesy of four wins, five draws and four defeats.

That was largely thanks to a solid home record, having only lost once in seven league outings at the Pirelli Stadium, most recently beating Leyton Orient 2-1, only to suffer consecutive away losses in their last two third-tier games.

A trip to Wycombe Wanderers ended in a 2-0 loss, before they followed up consecutive cup matches with a visit to MK Dons and suffered a 6-2 beating, having fallen 3-0 and 6-1 behind with goals from Emeka Adiele and Kain Adom nothing more than consolations.

Now sat 15th, but just two points off 11th-placed Leicester City, Burton Albion will bid to put those league defeats behind them and bounce back to winning ways at the Pirelli Stadium.

They face another tough test, though, as the visitors arrive aiming to continue an unbeaten run and narrow their gap to the league leaders.

In their first full season under Jack Wilshere, after falling agonisingly short in their playoff pursuit under him late last season, Luton Town currently sit fourth with 24 points on the board from 14 games.

The Hatters lost four of their first nine league games but have since bounced back in style, rebounding from the last of those with four straight wins over Barnsley, Leicester City, Doncaster Rovers and Peterborough United.

A trip to league leaders Huddersfield Town then followed, and Wilshere's men left with a creditable point from a 1-1 draw having led through Jordan Clark and been pegged back by Joe Taylor, before they hosted Forest Green Rovers in the FA Cup first round before the international break and won 2-0 with Emilio Lawrence and Clark on the scoresheet.

Now on the back of a free weekend last time out due to international call-ups, and a 3-0 EFL Trophy win over Peterborough United on Tuesday as Clark again scored alongside Nahki Wells and Devante Cole, Luton Town turn their focus back to League One and will hope to narrow their five-point gap to the top two with a fifth win in six league matches on Saturday.

Burton Albion are set to remain without Finn Delap, George Evans, Kyran Lofthouse and Caylan Vickers on Saturday due to injuries.

Matthew Dennis also missed their last game, and in his and Vickers's expected absence, Mark O'Mahony should again lead the line for the Brewers.

He should again have support from star man Charlie Webster and Kain Adom who scored against MK Dons last time out, while Kegs Chauke is a mainstay in midifeld.

Luton Town are still unable to call on the injured trio of Hakeem Odoffin, Gideon Kodua and Shayden Morris, who is yet to feature this season.

Wilshere fielded a strong starting XI for their midweek EFL Trophy tie with Peterborough and the Hatters will look similar on Saturday, with Wells continuing to lead the line having netted his ninth goal of the season in that win.

He will have support from Kasey Palmer and Jordan Clark, who also scored last time out to make it a goal in each of his last four games, while Dan Gore will hope to continue alongside midfield mainstay Liam Walsh despite Wilshere often fielding another attacking midfielder in League One action.

Burton Albion have seen their resilient start to the season halted in recent weeks, and we see them falling short against a strong Luton team who have won six of their last seven matches in all competitions.

#1785. Kovac backs Nwaneri to thrive amid ‘fierce competition’ at Dortmund

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Niko Kovac insisted Ethan Nwaneri will "play many more games" for Borussia Dortmund, but faces "fierce competition" for minutes.

Nwaneri joined BVB on loan in the summer from Arsenal, but has struggled to make his mark for the Bundesliga side in 2026-27.

The 19-year-old has made 12 appearances for Dortmund this season, with four of those coming as a starter, but is yet to record a direct goal contribution.

However, the teenager impressed for England's Under-21s during the international break, assisting twice in a win over France's Under-21s.

Kovac was impressed with Nwaneri's performances during the break, and has backed the Arsenal loanee to make an impact ahead of their trip to Borussia Monchengladbach on Saturday.

"We're delighted about that. It was a friendly in which he did really well. And that's why we signed him," Kovac said when asked about Nwaneri's display against France's U21s.

"We have some very good players in those attacking positions. Kosta [Karetsas] has also returned now. The competition is fierce.

"He [Nwaneri] has played a lot of games and, at just 19 years of age, he will certainly play many more games for us."

— Borussia Dortmund (@BlackYellow) November 18, 2026

Dortmund are second in the Bundesliga and are yet to lose in the competition this season.

They defeated Elversberg last time out, and Kovac wants to see a fast start against Gladbach following the international break.

"We can't afford to take any time to get going," added Kovac.

"There are still eight games left this year. In these games, we want to cement our place at the top of the Bundesliga. The other teams are pushing from behind. We have to be ready right away.

"The focus is on this game. It's plain and simple: we have to play our next opponent – Gladbach – in a way that ensures we win the game. Positive results build confidence and fuel the hunger for more."

Amid a season of struggles for Gladbach, wing-back Joe Scally has stood out for the Bundesliga's bottom side.

Among defenders in the competition this season, only Anthony Caci (six) has directly contributed to more goals than Scally (five – three goals, two assists).

Felix Nmecha scored his second brace of the Bundesliga season before the international break and has already equalled his personal best of four goals from the 2024-25 campaign.

However, Nmecha has scored 13 of his 14 total Bundesliga goals in home matches, with his only away goal coming in Eintracht Frankfurt in January 2026.

Dortmund have started a Bundesliga season unbeaten in nine games for only the fourth time, after 2002-03, 2018-19 and 2023-24 – in 2023-24, their first defeat came in their 10th match.

Across two seasons, Dortmund are unbeaten in 11 Bundesliga games, with their last defeat coming against their upcoming opponents Gladbach in early May (0-1 away).

Meanwhile, four points from nine matches is a new club-record low for Gladbach in the Bundesliga.

Of the 18 Bundesliga teams to have managed four points or fewer after nine games in the three-points-per-win era, only six avoided relegation (33%), most recently Mainz in the 2023-24 season.

However, Dortmund have won only one of their last six Bundesliga away games against Gladbach (D1 L4).

Since the start of the 2020-21 season, Dortmund have not lost more Bundesliga away games against any other side, while Gladbach have not celebrated more Bundesliga home wins against any other opponent in that time.

#1784. Eintracht Frankfurt vs Hoffenheim - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 23:51, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 08:45

Hoping to pick up where they left off in the Bundesliga, Hoffenheim will travel to face Eintracht Frankfurt at Deutsche Bank Park on Saturday.

Die Adler could make it four games unbeaten this weekend, though Die Kraichgauer are searching for back-to-back wins.

Adi Hutter's Frankfurt kicked off the 2026-27 campaign in lacklustre fashion, winning just one of their first four league outings, but they found their feet prior to the international break.

The 2-2 draw with SC Paderborn on November 7 may seem lacklustre on paper, but Die Adler were reduced to 10 men that day, and were still able to come from behind to snatch a point thanks to Jonathan Burkardt's 93rd-minute equaliser.

That stalemate left Hutter's side 10th in the table with 12 points, where they are level with Saturday's opponents and just three shy of the top six.

Additionally, Frankfurt have now lost just one of their last five matches across all competitions, winning three times in the process, including a pair of 3-1 victories over Hamburger SV, one at home in the league and one at Volksparkstadion in the DFB-Pokal.

However, Die Adler have conceded 20 goals in just nine top-flight games this term, giving them the joint third-worst defensive record in the Bundesliga, with only relegation-threatened Union Berlin (21) and Borussia Monchengladbach (25) letting in more so far.

Meanwhile, Christian Ilzer's Hoffenheim also struggled at the start of the season, but have stabilised amidst a potential resurgence.

Die Kraichgauer began with four defeats from their first five Bundesliga games, as well as six losses from their opening seven across all competitions, a dire return that had fans fearing the worst.

Thankfully for Ilzer's men, they were able to escape their shocking form with three consecutive victories in mid-October, including a 3-0 triumph over Ligue 1 giants Lyon in the Europa League and another 3-0 success against Bayer Leverkusen three days later.

Hoffenheim signed off for the international break by collecting all three points in a 2-1 win against Schalke 04 at SNP Arena, a performance inspired by Fisnik Asllani, who scored the opener before assisting Tim Lemperle's second with just 26 minutes on the clock.

As a result, Die Kraichgauer's European ambitions are alive again considering the club are currently ninth with 12 points, a mere three behind sixth-placed Werder Bremen.

Eintracht Frankfurt form (all competitions):

Frankfurt will be without striker Jessic Ngankam due to an adductor strain, while attacking midfielder Can Uzun is a doubt with illness, and will face a late fitness test.

If the latter is unavailable, then expect to see Noel Aseko-Nkili and Raphael Onyedika start in the centre of the park, flanked by Ritsu Doan and Fares Chaibi, who will be supporting a partnership of Jonathan Burkardt and Younes Ebnoutalib up top.

Elsewhere, versatile full-back Elias Baum is suspended after being sent off against Paderborn, though Ansgar Knauff and Keita Kosugi should be on hand to start either side of Robin Koch and Lilian Brassier.

As for Hoffenheim, they are missing Robin Hranac as he recovers from meniscus surgery, while fellow centre-back Albian Hajdari is a doubt with a plantar fascia injury, and right-back Valentin Gendrey is sidelined after suffering a fibula fracture late last month.

In their absence, Ilzer could opt for Koki Machida and Ozan Kabak at the heart of his defence once again, with Mats Rots and Vladimir Coufal at full-back.

Die Kraichgauer also have doubts about the fitness of midfielders Bambase Conte (groin) and Nathan De Cat (knee), as well as wingers Alexander Prass (thigh) and Patrick Wimmer (muscle).

If none of the four are ready to feature, then Leon Avdullahu and Wouter Burger look set to operate in the visitors' double pivot, platforming Andrej Kramaric, Fisnik Asllani and Adam Daghim behind striker Tim Lemperle.

Eintracht Frankfurt possible starting lineup:

Atubolu; Knauff, Koch, Brassier, Kosugi; Doan, Aseko-Nkili, Onyedika, Chaibi; Ebnoutalib, Burkardt

Baumann; Coufal, Machida, Kabak, Rots; Avdullahu, Burger; Kramaric, Asllani, Daghim; Lemperle

Frankfurt have scored eight goals in their last three matches, and have proven resilient in recent weeks.

However, Hoffenheim are likely to pose a threat given Die Adler's lack of defensive solidity, so expect to see a close-fought contest even if the hosts prevail.
